/tmp/skillplane-pr-quality-20260912/ski1.content: {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"id\":\"fc423036-f72e-487d-aa05-169c503d3a2a\",\"title\":\"Architecture & Delivery Plan — SKI-10: Remove duplicated framework and security primitives from Skillplane\",\"content\":\"# Architecture & Delivery Plan\\n\\nIssue: [SKI-10 — Remove duplicated framework and security primitives from Skillplane](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-10/remove-duplicated-framework-and-security-primitives-from-skillplane>)\\n\\n## Current-state constraints\\n\\n* Skillplane mounts AuthFn but shadows OTP send and verify with custom Hono handlers.\\n* The app implements a parallel auth browser client and response contract.\\n* Four AuthFn tables and a second expected-field list are maintained manually.\\n* OTP policy uses a local fixed-window persistence implementation.\\n* MCP pagination, domain search, and audit retrieval have separate signed-cursor implementations.\\n* MCP retrieval audit mapping duplicates an exported observability helper.\\n* The Cloudflare SendFn adapter is intentionally local but has parallel failure classes.\\n* DataFn adoption and McpFn migration are already tracked in <issue id=\\\"4056b3f8-de07-41bb-aad7-e3537d397b93\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-2/adopt-datafn-in-skillplanes-first-party-application-data-path\\\">SKI-2</issue> and <issue id=\\\"aaf7021f-756f-4919-ad1c-830c2fa250f8\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-mcp-regression-and-conformance-coverage\\\">SKI-6</issue>.\\n* The audit snapshot was static and package APIs must be reverified before implementation.\\n\\n## Proposed architecture\\n\\n### Authentication boundary\\n\\n```text\\nSvelte UI\\n  -> @authfn/client\\n    -> native AuthFn /otp/send and /otp/verify\\n      -> beforeChallengeSend\\n         - Turnstile validation\\n         - recipient rate policy\\n         - network rate policy\\n      -> AuthFn challenge/session persistence\\n      -> SendFn delivery adapter\\n```\\n\\nSkillplane owns policy inputs and product UX. AuthFn owns route validation, challenge lifecycle, verification, session issuance, envelopes, and client protocol.\\n\\nIf required response headers cannot be emitted by hooks, add narrowly scoped response middleware that observes the native response without reimplementing route logic.\\n\\n### Schema boundary\\n\\n```text\\nComposed AuthFn plugins\\n  -> superfunctions generate-schema\\n    -> reviewed Drizzle schema\\n      -> migration diff\\n      -> CI drift check\\n```\\n\\nGenerated output becomes the canonical AuthFn table shape. Skillplane retains database migrations and product-specific constraints, with explicit post-generation review.\\n\\n### Rate-limit boundary\\n\\nCompose the existing two-key policy over the shared persistent rate-limiter abstraction:\\n\\n* key A: normalized recipient;\\n* key B: privacy-preserving network identifier;\\n* policy: both checks must pass; failure is fail-closed;\\n* storage/counter algorithm: shared middleware;\\n* product mapping: Skillplane hook adapter.\\n\\nIf the shared adapter cannot meet the required transaction or Postgres behavior, document the incompatibility and propose the smallest upstream extension before retaining local storage.\\n\\n### Cursor boundary\\n\\nCreate one internal codec with an explicit payload envelope:\\n\\n* version;\\n* purpose;\\n* tenant/workspace binding;\\n* filter hash or canonical filter data;\\n* expiry;\\n* cursor position;\\n* signature.\\n\\nThe codec owns canonical base64url encoding, HMAC signing, constant-time verification, expiry checks, and payload validation. MCP, domain search, and audit surfaces retain thin adapters for their own error codes and payload types.\\n\\n### Audit boundary\\n\\nMove retrieval event construction to the existing central observability mapper. Extend the central writer with batch support only if needed so MCP does not reproduce transaction orchestration.\\n\\n### SendFn boundary\\n\\nKeep the Cloudflare Email Service provider in Skillplane for this issue. Replace custom provider and adapter error classes with SendFn-native `SendEmailResponse`, `EmailProviderError`, or `SendfnError` semantics supported by the exact installed version.\\n\\n## Component responsibilities\\n\\n| Component | Owns | Must not own |\\n| -- | -- | -- |\\n| AuthFn | OTP routes, validation, challenges, sessions, protocol client contract | Skillplane workspace/domain policy |\\n| Skillplane auth composition | Turnstile, recipient/network policy, UX mapping | Duplicate OTP lifecycle or client protocol |\\n| Schema generator | AuthFn table and plugin fields | Unreviewed destructive migrations |\\n| Shared middleware | Generic persistent rate-limit counters | Product-specific key and threshold policy |\\n| Internal cursor codec | Signing, encoding, verification, expiry | Surface-specific query semantics |\\n| Observability package | Retrieval-event mapping and persistence helpers | Product authorization decisions |\\n| Local Cloudflare SendFn adapter | Provider transport mapping | Parallel generic failure taxonomy |\\n\\n## Data and request flow\\n\\n### OTP send\\n\\n1. UI calls AuthFn client with normalized input and transient Turnstile evidence.\\n2. Native AuthFn route validates the protocol payload.\\n3. `beforeChallengeSend` verifies Turnstile and evaluates both rate-limit keys.\\n4. Policy-only transient data is removed before challenge metadata persists.\\n5. AuthFn invokes SendFn and returns its native response envelope.\\n6. Thin UI mapping presents success or a safe error.\\n\\n### OTP verify\\n\\n1. UI calls the native AuthFn verify method with cookie session mode.\\n2. AuthFn validates the challenge and issues the session.\\n3. Skillplane consumes the canonical result; it does not repeat protocol validation.\\n4. If a required pre-verify policy is unsupported, stop and design an upstream hook rather than shadowing the route.\\n\\n### Cursor verification\\n\\n1. Surface adapter supplies expected purpose, tenant, and filters.\\n2. Shared codec verifies signature and expiry.\\n3. Codec compares bound context and returns the typed position.\\n4. Surface maps failures to its protocol-specific error.\\n\\n## Security and privacy\\n\\n* Never persist or log Turnstile tokens.\\n* Retain fail-closed behavior for verification and rate-limit infrastructure failures.\\n* Use constant-time signature comparison.\\n* Bind cursors to purpose and tenant; bind filters where the surface is filter-sensitive.\\n* Rotate or version cursor secrets and payloads deliberately.\\n* Keep user-visible auth errors safe while preserving internal correlation.\\n* Review generated schema and migrations for accidental nullability, index, or constraint changes.\\n\\n## Reliability and observability\\n\\n* Emit distinct events for policy rejection, provider failure, invalid challenge, session failure, and internal failure.\\n* Preserve request correlation through native package extension points.\\n* Add metrics for OTP sends, policy rejects, provider failures, successful verifications, and cursor decode failures.\\n* Avoid logging recipient values where hashed or redacted dimensions suffice.\\n* Add batch audit persistence only behind a single transaction owner.\\n\\n## Migration and rollback\\n\\n* Land changes in small, reversible phases.\\n* Do not remove custom routes/client/schema until parity tests pass against native paths.\\n* If cursor compatibility is required, temporarily decode legacy versions and issue only the new version.\\n* If schema generation differs, inspect and stage migrations explicitly before changing runtime schema imports.\\n* Keep the old rate-limit table until shared persistence is proven and migration/cleanup is approved.\\n* Roll back by restoring the previous composition layer; do not roll back database state destructively.\\n\\n## Delivery phases\\n\\n1. **Version and contract verification**\\n   * Reverify released AuthFn, SendFn, and middleware versions and APIs.\\n   * Record the ownership matrix and exact parity requirements.\\n2. **AuthFn route/client migration**\\n   * Add released client dependency.\\n   * Move pre-send policy into supported hooks.\\n   * Switch UI calls to native routes.\\n   * Preserve cookie sessions, correlation, and required headers.\\n   * Remove shadows only after parity passes.\\n3. **Schema generation**\\n   * Generate from the composed plugin set.\\n   * Compare with current Drizzle definitions.\\n   * Review migration effects and add a CI drift gate.\\n4. **Rate-limit persistence**\\n   * Adapt the two-key policy to shared middleware.\\n   * Run concurrency, expiry, and failure-mode tests.\\n   * Remove generic local storage only after parity.\\n5. **Internal security consolidation**\\n   * Introduce the purpose-aware cursor codec.\\n   * Migrate MCP, search, and audit consumers.\\n   * Consolidate retrieval audit mapping and batch behavior.\\n6. **SendFn normalization**\\n   * Replace custom failure classes with native semantics.\\n   * Preserve the local provider boundary.\\n   * Add provider failure tests.\\n7. **Integrated validation and rollout**\\n   * Run typechecks, unit/integration tests, browser-critical auth flows, database migration checks, and MCP regression.\\n   * Decide legacy cursor compatibility.\\n   * Roll out with auth and error telemetry monitored.\\n\\n## Validation plan\\n\\n* Unit tests for hook policy, cursor codec, error adapters, and generated-schema drift.\\n* Hono integration tests proving native AuthFn endpoints and cookie-session behavior.\\n* Browser E2E for OTP send, invalid code, expired code, success, rate limit, Turnstile failure, and provider failure.\\n* Database tests for concurrent rate limits and schema migration safety.\\n* MCP and audit pagination tests across purpose, tenant, filter, expiry, and tamper cases.\\n* SendFn adapter tests for native success and failure shapes.\\n* Static reachability checks that fail if the app restores a parallel AuthFn client or OTP route shadow.\\n\\n## Dependencies\\n\\n* [SKI-1 — Move service-principal credential authentication to AuthFn API keys](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-1/move-service-principal-credential-authentication-to-authfn-api-keys>)\\n* [SKI-2 — Adopt DataFn in Skillplane's first-party application data path](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-2/adopt-datafn-in-skillplanes-first-party-application-data-path>)\\n* [SKI-6 — Adopt McpFn for MCP regression and conformance coverage](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-mcp-regression-and-conformance-coverage>)\\n* Released AuthFn client/Svelte packages, schema generator, Superfunctions middleware, and SendFn package at implementation-time verified versions.\\n\\n## Risks and tradeoffs\\n\\n* Native AuthFn behavior may differ subtly from current response envelopes.\\n* Missing hooks could tempt route shadowing; prefer an upstream extension proposal.\\n* Cursor consolidation can invalidate in-flight pages.\\n* Generated schema may reveal drift requiring careful migration.\\n* Shared rate-limit persistence may not map cleanly to the current database adapter.\\n* A broad refactor could obscure regressions; phase work by boundary and retain explicit parity gates.\\n\\n## Alternatives\\n\\n* Keep all local implementations: lowest immediate change, highest ongoing drift.\\n* Upstream every Skillplane policy into Superfunctions: rejected because product-specific concerns would pollute generic packages.\\n* Perform one large replacement branch: rejected because rollback and attribution would be poor.\\n* Defer all work to McpFn/DataFn migrations: rejected because AuthFn, schema, cursor, audit, and SendFn duplication are independently actionable now.\\n\\n## Assumptions and open questions\\n\\n* **Assumption:** Exact package APIs remain compatible with the audited versions; verify before implementation.\\n* **Open question:** Header extension point for native OTP responses.\\n* **Open question:** Legacy cursor compatibility window.\\n* **Open question:** Shared middleware adapter fit and any upstream change.\\n* **Open question:** Whether browser auth state benefits from `@authfn/svelte` beyond `@authfn/client`.\\n* **Open question:** Timing and ownership of upstreaming the Cloudflare provider.\\n\\n## Completion evidence\\n\\nCompletion requires source and test evidence for every acceptance criterion. A green focused suite does not by itself prove deployed behavior; local, browser, database, tunnel, and deployed verification must be reported separately.\",\"icon\":null,\"color\":null,\"url\":\"https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-10-remove-duplicated-framework-and-58a68c622bf3\",\"slugId\":\"58a68c622bf3\",\"createdAt\":\"2026-08-22T05:52:37.647Z\",\"updatedAt\":\"2026-08-22T05:52:38.800Z\",\"archivedAt\":null,\"creator\":{\"id\":\"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a\",\"name\":\"Aravind\"},\"updatedBy\":{\"id\":\"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a\",\"name\":\"Aravind\"},\"project\":null,\"initiative\":null,\"team\":null,\"issue\":{\"id\":\"SKI-10\",\"title\":\"Remove duplicated framework and security primitives from Skillplane\"}}"}]}

Workspace authorization, skill publication, immutable bundles, OAuth authorization-server behavior, audit retention, and authorization-aware search remain legitimate Skillplane responsibilities. The problem is duplicated generic behavior that can drift from the packages already selected as canonical.\\n\\nThe largest user-facing risk is authentication drift: Skillplane shadows AuthFn OTP routes and implements a parallel browser client. The other findings primarily increase security review cost, migration risk, and maintenance burden.\\n\\n## Target users and stakeholders\\n\\n* Skillplane end users who need reliable OTP login and stable sessions.\\n* MCP clients and service principals that depend on consistent authorization and error behavior.\\n* Skillplane engineers maintaining product logic and migrations.\\n* Superfunctions maintainers responsible for reusable AuthFn, SendFn, middleware, and schema-generation contracts.\\n* Operators reviewing security, rate limiting, auditability, and incident behavior.\\n\\n## Use cases and journeys\\n\\n### OTP sign-in\\n\\n1. A user enters an email in Skillplane.\\n2. Skillplane invokes the released AuthFn client.\\n3. AuthFn owns request validation, challenge issuance, verification, and session behavior.\\n4. Skillplane policy runs through supported hooks: Turnstile validation and recipient/network rate limits.\\n5. A successful verification establishes the expected cookie session without a parallel response contract.\\n\\n### Schema evolution\\n\\n1. The composed AuthFn plugin set is the source of schema truth.\\n2. The Superfunctions generator emits deterministic Drizzle schema.\\n3. Reviewers inspect the generated migration.\\n4. CI fails when committed schema and generated output drift.\\n\\n### Pagination and audit retrieval\\n\\n1. A product surface requests a page with filters.\\n2. One internal cursor codec signs purpose, tenant, filters, and expiry.\\n3. Protocol-specific adapters map codec failures to Hono, MCP, or domain errors.\\n4. Retrieval events use one central mapping before persistence.\\n\\n### Email delivery failure\\n\\n1. AuthFn requests OTP delivery through the local Cloudflare SendFn adapter.\\n2. The adapter returns or throws SendFn-native failure semantics.\\n3. AuthFn and Skillplane map the canonical error without parallel custom classes.\\n\\n## Ideas discussed\\n\\n* Use native AuthFn OTP routes rather than Hono route shadows.\\n* Replace the custom browser auth client with `@authfn/client`; use `@authfn/svelte` only where its state bindings add value.\\n* Move Turnstile and two-key rate-limit policy into `beforeChallengeSend`; retain only minimal additive middleware if response headers cannot be expressed by the hook.\\n* Generate AuthFn schema from the composed plugin set.\\n* Compose product-specific recipient/network policy over shared rate-limit persistence.\\n* Consolidate three cursor implementations into one purpose-aware codec.\\n* Reuse the exported retrieval audit mapper.\\n* Keep the local Cloudflare provider for now, but normalize it to SendFn contracts.\\n* Track DataFn and McpFn separately in <issue id=\\\"4056b3f8-de07-41bb-aad7-e3537d397b93\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-2/adopt-datafn-in-skillplanes-first-party-application-data-path\\\">SKI-2</issue> and <issue id=\\\"aaf7021f-756f-4919-ad1c-830c2fa250f8\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-mcp-regression-and-conformance-coverage\\\">SKI-6</issue>.\\n\\n## Desired outcomes and success measures\\n\\n* No local owner for AuthFn OTP send or verify routes.\\n* No parallel browser implementation of the AuthFn protocol.\\n* Authentication parity tests prove cookie sessions, validation, fail-closed policy, and safe Turnstile handling.\\n* Generated AuthFn schema has a reproducible drift gate.\\n* Only one cursor-signing implementation remains.\\n* Retrieval audit mapping has one canonical owner.\\n* SendFn failures have one error contract.\\n* The reduction in duplicate code does not move Skillplane-specific invariants into generic packages.\\n\\n## Decisions and rationale\\n\\n* **Decision:** Keep this issue separate from DataFn adoption.\\n  **Rationale:** <issue id=\\\"4056b3f8-de07-41bb-aad7-e3537d397b93\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-2/adopt-datafn-in-skillplanes-first-party-application-data-path\\\">SKI-2</issue> already captures DataFn reachability and read/command ownership.\\n* **Decision:** Keep McpFn migration separate.\\n  **Rationale:** <issue id=\\\"aaf7021f-756f-4919-ad1c-830c2fa250f8\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-mcp-regression-and-conformance-coverage\\\">SKI-6</issue> already captures it, and the audited package was not available at the checked npm identifier.\\n* **Decision:** Preserve the local Cloudflare provider initially.\\n  **Rationale:** Local placement was an accepted boundary around overlapping external work; error-contract normalization can happen without an upstream write.\\n* **Decision:** Preserve Skillplane's OAuth authorization-server plugin.\\n  **Rationale:** AuthFn social OAuth and resource-server middleware do not replace consent, authorization-code issuance, refresh-family rotation, and workspace policy.\\n* **Decision:** Prefer hooks/plugins/clients over route overrides.\\n  **Rationale:** This keeps validation, session, and protocol behavior on the package's supported upgrade path.\\n\\n## Rejected alternatives and tradeoffs\\n\\n* **Keep route shadows because they currently work:** rejected as the default because it preserves duplicated validation, envelopes, request IDs, and error mapping.\\n* **Move all auth policy into AuthFn core:** rejected because Turnstile and product-specific recipient/network policy belong in consumer composition unless a broadly reusable hook is missing.\\n* **Replace all Hono/domain APIs with DataFn:** rejected; invariant-heavy commands remain domain workflows.\\n* **Replace all Skillplane storage/search code with FileFn/SearchFn immediately:** rejected pending fit tests for immutable canonical bundles and authorization-filtered search.\\n* **Bundle McpFn migration into this issue:** rejected to avoid mixing a larger transport/registry modernization with current released-package corrections.\\n\\n## Product, UX, and operational considerations\\n\\n* OTP response and error behavior must remain understandable and stable for the UI.\\n* Rate-limit headers may be useful for diagnostics but must not require ownership of the entire OTP route.\\n* Cursor invalidation can affect pagination continuity after deployment; the rollout decision must be explicit.\\n* Schema regeneration must be reviewed like a migration, not treated as a formatting change.\\n* Observability must distinguish policy rejection, provider failure, invalid OTP, and internal failure without logging secrets or raw Turnstile tokens.\\n\\n## Goals\\n\\n* Reduce duplicate framework and security logic.\\n* Make package ownership explicit and upgradeable.\\n* Preserve product-specific security policy and domain invariants.\\n* Add evidence that production surfaces traverse the intended integration.\\n\\n## Non-goals\\n\\n* <issue id=\\\"4056b3f8-de07-41bb-aad7-e3537d397b93\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-2/adopt-datafn-in-skillplanes-first-party-application-data-path\\\">SKI-2</issue> DataFn application adoption.\\n* <issue id=\\\"693fecfe-0647-47d3-a152-20874fb3fad5\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-1/move-service-principal-credential-authentication-to-authfn-api-keys\\\">SKI-1</issue> service-principal API-key work.\\n* <issue id=\\\"aaf7021f-756f-4919-ad1c-830c2fa250f8\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-mcp-regression-and-conformance-coverage\\\">SKI-6</issue> McpFn adoption.\\n* Upstream package changes without separate authorization.\\n* Product redesign, staffing, dates, estimates, or deployment commitments.\\n\\n## Assumptions\\n\\n* **Assumption:** The released package versions still expose the APIs observed in the audit; implementation must reverify exact versions.\\n* **Assumption:** Native AuthFn routes support the required cookie-session mode.\\n* **Assumption:** A minimal response middleware can preserve required headers if AuthFn hooks cannot emit them.\\n\\n## Open questions\\n\\n* Is an upstream AuthFn response hook preferable to thin additive middleware?\\n* Must already-issued cursors remain valid across migration?\\n* Does shared rate-limit persistence support the current Postgres adapter directly?\\n* Which parity tests should be browser-level versus Hono integration tests?\\n* Should the Cloudflare provider be upstreamed after local normalization?\\n\\n## Acceptance criteria\\n\\n* The acceptance criteria in <issue id=\\\"829274d3-c021-40ad-8082-91911d541592\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-10/remove-duplicated-framework-and-security-primitives-from-skillplane\\\">SKI-10</issue> are met and read back from tests and source.\\n* No Turnstile token is stored in challenge metadata or logs.\\n* Package-owned and Skillplane-owned responsibilities are documented.\\n* <issue id=\\\"693fecfe-0647-47d3-a152-20874fb3fad5\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-1/move-service-principal-credential-authentication-to-authfn-api-keys\\\">SKI-1</issue>, <issue id=\\\"4056b3f8-de07-41bb-aad7-e3537d397b93\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-2/adopt-datafn-in-skillplanes-first-party-application-data-path\\\">SKI-2</issue>, and <issue id=\\\"aaf7021f-756f-4919-ad1c-830c2fa250f8\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-mcp-regression-and-conformance-coverage\\\">SKI-6</issue> remain separate related work rather than being silently absorbed.\",\"icon\":null,\"color\":null,\"url\":\"https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-10-remove-duplicated-framework-and-6b49cd027863\",\"slugId\":\"6b49cd027863\",\"createdAt\":\"2026-08-22T05:52:34.996Z\",\"updatedAt\":\"2026-08-22T05:52:35.899Z\",\"archivedAt\":null,\"creator\":{\"id\":\"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a\",\"name\":\"Aravind\"},\"updatedBy\":{\"id\":\"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a\",\"name\":\"Aravind\"},\"project\":null,\"initiative\":null,\"team\":null,\"issue\":{\"id\":\"SKI-10\",\"title\":\"Remove duplicated framework and security primitives from Skillplane\"}}"}]}

This is current-head quality, not an original-submission/model benchmark. ## Findings ### F19-1 · P1 · Configure the native client's Skillplane CSRF cookie prefix The client at [client.ts:28](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/app/src/lib/auth/client.ts#L28) omits `cookiePrefix: "skillplane"` and [signOut:80](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/app/src/lib/auth/client.ts#L80) removes the old explicit CSRF header. The installed @authfn/client@0.2.0 infers the prefix only from a session cookie. AuthFn makes that cookie HttpOnly, so browser JavaScript sees `skillplane.csrf` but not the session cookie; the client falls back to `authfn.csrf` and omits x-authfn-csrf. The server's assertValidCsrf rejects authenticated sign-out without that header, leaving the session active. **Evidence:** actual app signOut wrapper + released client with realistic readable cookie and mocked fetch produced a null header instead of the sentinel. Cookie issuance and server validation were code-traced. No live logout was performed. **Fix:** configure the prefix explicitly and add a browser-realistic logout regression with the session cookie hidden. ### F19-2 · P2 · Migrate the production OTP verification consumer The new hook reads only [metadata.turnstileToken:18](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/packages/auth/src/otp-policy.ts#L18), but [verify-email-production.mjs:65](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/scripts/verify-email-production.mjs#L65) still sends a top-level token and requires accepted/expiresInSeconds. Native send returns challengeId/sent. The later verify request also omits the explicit cookie session mode that the old route supplied. **Impact:** the documented Turnstile-based production verification command cannot complete its OTP flow. **Evidence:** executing the actual script with a dummy recipient/token and mocked fetch captures no metadata.turnstileToken. Response and verification requirements were traced through the script and released OTP plugin. **Fix:** migrate request, native success checks and cookie-session verification together; test both stages with mocked external calls. ### F19-3 · P2 · Keep schema preflight executable on the declared minimum Node [check-authfn-schema.mjs:12](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/scripts/check-authfn-schema.mjs#L12) dynamically imports TypeScript from plain node. package.json declares Node >=22.13.0, but this invocation fails there before checking the schema. **Evidence:** Node 22.13.0 exits 1 with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION for plugin-composition.ts. pages.content:
**Historical snapshot:** This was the head open at review start. A new commit was merged during this task; consult the separate merged-head follow-up before treating these findings as current. **7.5/10 — Needs fixes.** The removed helpers and barrel exports have no remaining runtime callers; active domain transactions, MCP audit writes, and TestObjectStorage are retained. ## Decision and scope [PR #15](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/pull/15) · reviewed head `b155d44c2309fc460f0946a7c05741808c1974b2` · base and merge base `b4c69559c7eaf9174baae39a8b4279b55643520a`. No owning Linear issue or design link was found in PR metadata/conversation. Fidelity is assessed against the explicit no-product-behavior-change PR promise and the base API contract. Full author transcripts were not retrieved. ## Weighted quality
DimensionWeightScoreRationale
Issue/design fidelity30%7/10The no-behavior-change promise is broken by query precedence.
Correctness and safety30%7/10One reproduced versioned API regression.
Architecture and maintainability20%9/10Small, well-scoped removal of genuinely unused code.
Verification quality15%7/1076 unit tests pass, but new integration assertions encode changed semantics.
Delivery completeness5%8/10Private package export cleanup is consistent; PR body still contains stale summaries.
Scores are rounded to the nearest 0.5; blockers override the average. This is current-head quality, not an original-submission/model benchmark. ## Findings ### F15-1 · P2 · Restore the historical false/state precedence At [skills.ts:95](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/b155d44c2309fc460f0946a7c05741808c1974b2/packages/api/src/routes/skills.ts#L95), requests combining `includeArchived=false` with `state=archived` or `state=all` now force active-only results. The base version used `state` for both false and absent legacy flags. Both listing and search silently omit the requested archived records. **Evidence:** four HTTP route probes fail at this head (actual active instead of archived/all); the same probes pass 4/4 against the base route. The current head fixes provider-cause redaction, forwards retrieval fencing epochs, distinguishes Turnstile outages, and shares plugin composition. Architecture explicitly says generate from the composed plugin set, compare existing Drizzle definitions, and preserve consumer parity before removing shadows. Initial probe setup failures (missing generated Svelte tsconfig and a too-short dummy token) were corrected and excluded from findings. ## Weighted quality
DimensionWeightScoreRationale

Scores are rounded to the nearest 0.5; blockers override the average. This is current-head quality, not an original-submission/model benchmark. ## Findings ### F19-1 · P1 · Configure the native client's Skillplane CSRF cookie prefix The client at [client.ts:28](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/app/src/lib/auth/client.ts#L28) omits `cookiePrefix: "skillplane"` and [signOut:80](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/app/src/lib/auth/client.ts#L80) removes the old explicit CSRF header. The installed @authfn/client@0.2.0 infers the prefix only from a session cookie. AuthFn makes that cookie HttpOnly, so browser JavaScript sees `skillplane.csrf` but not the session cookie; the client falls back to `authfn.csrf` and omits x-authfn-csrf. The server's assertValidCsrf rejects authenticated sign-out without that header, leaving the session active. **Evidence:** actual app signOut wrapper + released client with realistic readable cookie and mocked fetch produced a null header instead of the sentinel. Cookie issuance and server validation were code-traced. No live logout was performed. **Fix:** configure the prefix explicitly and add a browser-realistic logout regression with the session cookie hidden. ### F19-2 · P2 · Migrate the production OTP verification consumer The new hook reads only [metadata.turnstileToken:18](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/packages/auth/src/otp-policy.ts#L18), but [verify-email-production.mjs:65](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/scripts/verify-email-production.mjs#L65) still sends a top-level token and requires accepted/expiresInSeconds. Native send returns challengeId/sent. The later verify request omits an explicit cookie session mode, but the released server defaults it to cookie; that omission is not a separate defect. **Impact:** the documented Turnstile-based production verification command cannot complete its OTP flow. **Evidence:** executing the actual script with a dummy recipient/token and mocked fetch captures no metadata.turnstileToken. Response and verification requirements were traced through the script and released OTP plugin. **Fix:** migrate request, native success checks and cookie-session verification together; test both stages with mocked external calls. ### F19-3 · P2 · Keep schema preflight executable on the declared minimum Node [check-authfn-schema.mjs:12](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/scripts/check-authfn-schema.mjs#L12) dynamically imports TypeScript from plain node. package.json declares Node >=22.13.0, but this invocation fails there before checking the schema. **Evidence:** Node 22.13.0 exits 1 with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION for plugin-composition.ts. Node 22.22.1 exits 0 with the committed digest. **Fix:** use a supported loader/flag or built JavaScript across the declared range, or deliberately raise and document the minimum; verify the minimum version. ### F19-4 · P2 · Compare generated schema with the actual Drizzle schema [check-authfn-schema.mjs:31](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/scripts/check-authfn-schema.mjs#L31) hashes the AuthFn schema description but never generates or compares [the manually maintained Drizzle schema](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/packages/db/src/schema/authfn.ts). This does detect upstream/plugin description drift, but does not fulfill SKI-10's generated-schema parity requirement. **Evidence:** in a temporary copy, changing the actual users primary-email column to WRONG_primary_email still produces the same successful schema check and digest (exit 0); the temporary change was restored. **Fix:** deterministically generate the composed Drizzle output, compare it to committed runtime schema and review migration effects. A lock of the abstract description alone is insufficient. ### Remaining issue scope Cursor consolidation is explicitly deferred in the PR; separate HMAC mechanics remain in domain search and audit pagination. Keep SKI-10 open and explicitly track the remaining phase. The PR's automated “closing out SKI-10” summary contradicts its own scope note. ## Validation and coverage 34 existing focused auth/email/observability/MCP audit tests in 14 files passed; auth package TypeScript passed. Two independent consumer regression assertions fail for the missing CSRF header and stale production token shape. Schema check passes on Node 22.22.1 and fails on 22.13.0; a temporary Drizzle-drift mutation passes the gate incorrectly. Database integration/security flows, full build/release gates, real-browser OTP/logout and deployed behavior remain unrun. Dependencies were reused, not installed cleanly; npx fetched Node 22.13.0 for the compatibility probe. CI at capture: security/reviewer checks mostly successful; Sourcery skipped. SonarCloud analysis was CANCELLED and its conversation comment reports a failed analysis. CodeRabbit also reports review-rate exhaustion. No hosted product build/test gate was shown in the fetched rollup; bot success does not establish release readiness. ## Review-surface triage 25 threads / 29 thread comments, 12 review bodies and 8 conversation comments captured with pagination complete. Fencing epoch, raw provider cause, outage classification, schema plugin omission, idempotency freshness and stale status-field findings are fixed. Production consumer and minimum-Node findings remain current; duplicates are grouped. The hard-coded 600-second UI TTL comment is not adopted as a current defect because the released send response lacks expiresInSeconds and the configured/default lifetime remains 600. Incomplete error-body type guarding is unverified hardening without a malformed native producer. The turnstile_ prefix replacement is a P3 maintainability observation, not evidence of replay reuse. ## Implementation authorship Original 832abaef… is attributed to Tembo / Codex / gpt-5.6-sol / high by the live PR badge (medium confidence, not execution metadata); linked session b862a939-eda2-465a-ac45-639b93c87e38. ## Current finding status
- **F19-1 · P1 · Still open:** native browser sign-out omits x-authfn-csrf with the realistic readable cookie `skillplane.csrf`. The actual app wrapper + released client probe still fails (null header instead of dummy-csrf). Configure `cookiePrefix: "skillplane"` in [client.ts:28](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/2b97525ddbd69efaf6af2fb9b7bf7b2049318a34/app/src/lib/auth/client.ts#L28). The HttpOnly session cookie cannot be used by JavaScript to infer the prefix; authenticated server sign-out requires the header. Public client path was executed with mocked fetch; server rejection is code-traced, not a live logout claim.
- **F19-2 · Fixed:** production verifier now sends metadata.turnstileToken, validates challengeId/sent, and explicitly requests cookie mode. Independent request-shape probe passes; the two new script tests pass. Native cookie mode was already the default, so its former omission was not independently a defect.
- **F19-3 · Fixed:** package scripts now use --experimental-strip-types. The actual schema command passes on Node 22.13.0.
- **F19-4 · P2 · Still open:** [schema gate](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/2b97525ddbd69efaf6af2fb9b7bf7b2049318a34/scripts/check-authfn-schema.mjs#L30) still hashes an abstract AuthFn description without generating/comparing the runtime Drizzle schema. A temporary wrong-column probe at the initial head passed the gate; relevant gate and Drizzle source are unchanged at this head. Deterministic generation/parity remains required by SKI-10. This is a missing drift guarantee, not a claim that a wrong column currently ships.

## Other fixes and integration
Current changes validate all required error-envelope fields, restore private unmatched-route 404s, test retry timing, and use plain UUID Turnstile idempotency keys. The active retrievalAuditEvent helper/export survives integration of PR #15. Inherited changes from already merged #18 were reviewed separately; inherited #17 changes were not fully re-audited in this bounded follow-up.

## Validation and score
42 focused auth/email/observability/MCP audit tests pass in 14 files, plus 2 production-script tests. Independent consumer probes: 1 pass (production metadata), 1 failure (sign-out CSRF). Node 22.13.0 schema invocation passes. Dependencies reused from existing worktree; source comes from an immutable extraction of the final PR head. No real-browser, database integration/security, full build/release or deployment verification ran.

Provisional dimensions: fidelity 6, correctness 6.5, architecture 7.5, verification 7, delivery 6; weights 30/30/20/15/5, rounded to 6.5. Keep SKI-10 open for generated-schema parity and deferred cursor consolidation. This is a targeted merged-head refresh, not a new full audit of all inherited main changes.

import { it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
it('browser sign-out forwards the readable Skillplane CSRF cookie', async () => {

});

## Setup and source identity
At a clean checkout of the exact SHA, install the pinned pnpm lockfile with Node 22.22.1. This review reused corresponding PR worktree dependencies, not a clean install. Source aliases point all @skillplane imports into the immutable extracted snapshot. No dirty worktree source was used. For the app client, generate SvelteKit types before running (this review reused generated .svelte-kit configuration). No database or production service was contacted by the probes.

## Minimal config
Save probes.config.mjs at repository root:
```javascript
import {readdirSync,readFileSync} from 'node:fs';
import {resolve} from 'node:path';
const alias={};
for(const name of readdirSync('packages')){
 try {const p=JSON.parse(readFileSync('packages/'+name+'/package.json','utf8'));alias[p.name]=resolve('packages',name,'src/index.ts');}catch{}
}
alias.hono=resolve('packages/api/node_modules/hono/dist/index.js');
export default {resolve:{alias},test:{include:['review-probes.test.ts'],maxWorkers:1}};
```
## Probe source
Save review-probes.test.ts at repository root, then run `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config probes.config.mjs`.
```typescript
import { it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
it('browser sign-out forwards the readable Skillplane CSRF cookie', async () => {
  vi.stubGlobal('document', {cookie:'skillplane.csrf=dummy-csrf'});
  const sent: RequestInit[] = [];
  vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn(async (_url, init) => {
    sent.push(init);
    return Response.json({ok:true,data:{signedOut:true},requestId:'probe'});
  }));
  const { signOut } = await import('./app/src/lib/auth/client.ts');
  await signOut();
  expect(new Headers(sent[0]?.headers).get('x-authfn-csrf')).toBe('dummy-csrf');
});
it('production verifier sends a token using the native metadata contract', async () => {
  vi.stubEnv('SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_OTP_RECIPIENT','probe@example.test');
  vi.stubEnv('SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_TURNSTILE_TOKEN','dummy-turnstile-0123456789012345');
  vi.stubEnv('SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_OTP_CODE','');
  const sent: unknown[] = [];
  vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn(async (_url, init) => {
    sent.push(JSON.parse(init.body));
    return Response.json({ok:false,error:{code:'AUTHFN_RATE_LIMITED'},requestId:'probe'}, {status:429,headers:{'cache-control':'private, no-store','x-request-id':'probe'}});
  }));
  delete process.env.SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_OTP_CODE;
  const {verifyProductionEmail} = await import('./scripts/verify-email-production.mjs');
  await verifyProductionEmail().catch(()=>{});
  expect(sent).toHaveLength(1);
  expect(sent[0]).toHaveProperty('metadata.turnstileToken','dummy-turnstile-0123456789012345');
});

```

Two independent consumer regression assertions fail for the missing CSRF header and stale production token shape. Schema check passes on Node 22.22.1 and fails on 22.13.0; a temporary Drizzle-drift mutation passes the gate incorrectly. Database integration/security flows, full build/release gates, real-browser OTP/logout and deployed behavior remain unrun. Dependencies were reused, not installed cleanly; npx fetched Node 22.13.0 for the compatibility probe.

Merged head: 42 existing tests pass; two production-script node tests pass. Independent consumer probes: one passes (production metadata), one fails (CSRF header). The existing suite selection was packages/auth/src, packages/email/src, packages/email/tests/security, packages/observability/src and mcp/src/audit.test.ts with source aliases.

## Setup and source identity
At a clean checkout of the exact SHA, install the pinned pnpm lockfile with Node 22.22.1. This review reused corresponding PR worktree dependencies, not a clean install. Source aliases point all @skillplane imports into the immutable extracted snapshot. No dirty worktree source was used. ```javascript
import {readdirSync,readFileSync} from 'node:fs';
import {resolve} from 'node:path';

 try {const p=JSON.parse(readFileSync('packages/'+name+'/package.json','utf8'));alias[p.name]=resolve('packages',name,'src/index.ts');}catch{}

Save review-probes.test.ts at repository root, then run `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config probes.config.mjs`.
```typescript
import { it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
it('browser sign-out forwards the readable Skillplane CSRF cookie', async () => {
  vi.stubGlobal('document', {cookie:'skillplane.csrf=dummy-csrf'});
  const sent: RequestInit[] = [];
  vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn(async (_url, init) => {
    sent.push(init);
    return Response.json({ok:true,data:{signedOut:true},requestId:'probe'});
  }));
  const { signOut } = await import('./app/src/lib/auth/client.ts');
  await signOut();
  expect(new Headers(sent[0]?.headers).get('x-authfn-csrf')).toBe('dummy-csrf');
});
it('production verifier sends a token using the native metadata contract', async () => {
  vi.stubEnv('SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_OTP_RECIPIENT','probe@example.test');
  vi.stubEnv('SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_TURNSTILE_TOKEN','dummy-turnstile-0123456789012345');
  vi.stubEnv('SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_OTP_CODE','');
  const sent: unknown[] = [];
  vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn(async (_url, init) => {
    sent.push(JSON.parse(init.body));
    return Response.json({ok:false,error:{code:'AUTHFN_RATE_LIMITED'},requestId:'probe'}, {status:429,headers:{'cache-control':'private, no-store','x-request-id':'probe'}});
  }));
  delete process.env.SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_OTP_CODE;
  const {verifyProductionEmail} = await import('./scripts/verify-email-production.mjs');
  await verifyProductionEmail().catch(()=>{});
  expect(sent).toHaveLength(1);
  expect(sent[0]).toHaveProperty('metadata.turnstileToken','dummy-turnstile-0123456789012345');
});

**6.5/10 provisional — needs fixes despite having merged.**
Reviewed head `2b97525ddbd69efaf6af2fb9b7bf7b2049318a34`, merged at 2026-09-12T17:09:26Z; merge commit `ad4308fa1f5bb3bfff043993ea162190d9375345`.
## Current finding status
- **F19-1 · P1 · Still open:** native browser sign-out omits x-authfn-csrf with the realistic readable cookie `skillplane.csrf`. The actual app wrapper + released client probe still fails (null header instead of dummy-csrf). Configure `cookiePrefix: "skillplane"` in [client.ts:28](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/2b97525ddbd69efaf6af2fb9b7bf7b2049318a34/app/src/lib/auth/client.ts#L28). The HttpOnly session cookie cannot be used by JavaScript to infer the prefix; authenticated server sign-out requires the header. Public client path was executed with mocked fetch; server rejection is code-traced, not a live logout claim.
- **F19-2 · Fixed:** production verifier now sends metadata.turnstileToken, validates challengeId/sent, and explicitly requests cookie mode. Independent request-shape probe passes; the two new script tests pass. Native cookie mode was already the default, so its former omission was not independently a defect.
- **F19-3 · Fixed:** package scripts now use --experimental-strip-types. The actual schema command passes on Node 22.13.0.

A temporary wrong-column probe at the initial head passed the gate; relevant gate and Drizzle source are unchanged at this head. Deterministic generation/parity remains required by SKI-10. This is a missing drift guarantee, not a claim that a wrong column currently ships.

Current changes validate all required error-envelope fields, restore private unmatched-route 404s, test retry timing, and use plain UUID Turnstile idempotency keys. The active retrievalAuditEvent helper/export survives integration of PR #15. Node 22.13.0 schema invocation passes. Dependencies reused from existing worktree; source comes from an immutable extraction of the final PR head. No real-browser, database integration/security, full build/release or deployment verification ran.

Keep SKI-10 open for generated-schema parity and deferred cursor consolidation. This is a targeted merged-head refresh, not a new full audit of all inherited main changes.

This is current-head quality, not an original-submission/model benchmark. ## Findings ### F19-1 · P1 · Configure the native client's Skillplane CSRF cookie prefix The client at [client.ts:28](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/app/src/lib/auth/client.ts#L28) omits `cookiePrefix: "skillplane"` and [signOut:80](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/app/src/lib/auth/client.ts#L80) removes the old explicit CSRF header. The installed @authfn/client@0.2.0 infers the prefix only from a session cookie. AuthFn makes that cookie HttpOnly, so browser JavaScript sees `skillplane.csrf` but not the session cookie; the client falls back to `authfn.csrf` and omits x-authfn-csrf. The server's assertValidCsrf rejects authenticated sign-out without that header, leaving the session active. **Evidence:** actual app signOut wrapper + released client with realistic readable cookie and mocked fetch produced a null header instead of the sentinel. Cookie issuance and server validation were code-traced. No live logout was performed. **Fix:** configure the prefix explicitly and add a browser-realistic logout regression with the session cookie hidden. ### F19-2 · P2 · Migrate the production OTP verification consumer The new hook reads only [metadata.turnstileToken:18](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/packages/auth/src/otp-policy.ts#L18), but [verify-email-production.mjs:65](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/scripts/verify-email-production.mjs#L65) still sends a top-level token and requires accepted/expiresInSeconds. Native send returns challengeId/sent. The later verify request omits an explicit cookie session mode, but the released server defaults it to cookie; that omission is not a separate defect. **Impact:** the documented Turnstile-based production verification command cannot complete its OTP flow. **Evidence:** executing the actual script with a dummy recipient/token and mocked fetch captures no metadata.turnstileToken. Response and verification requirements were traced through the script and released OTP plugin. **Fix:** migrate request, native success checks and cookie-session verification together; test both stages with mocked external calls. ### F19-3 · P2 · Keep schema preflight executable on the declared minimum Node [check-authfn-schema.mjs:12](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/scripts/check-authfn-schema.mjs#L12) dynamically imports TypeScript from plain node. package.json declares Node \>=22.13.0, but this invocation fails there before checking the schema. **Evidence:** Node 22.13.0 exits 1 with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION for plugin-composition.ts. Node 22.22.1 exits 0 with the committed digest. **Fix:** use a supported loader/flag or built JavaScript across the declared range, or deliberately raise and document the minimum; verify the minimum version. ### F19-4 · P2 · Compare generated schema with the actual Drizzle schema [check-authfn-schema.mjs:31](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/scripts/check-authfn-schema.mjs#L31) hashes the AuthFn schema description but never generates or compares [the manually maintained Drizzle schema](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/packages/db/src/schema/authfn.ts). This does detect upstream/plugin description drift, but does not fulfill SKI-10's generated-schema parity requirement. **Evidence:** in a temporary copy, changing the actual users primary-email column to WRONG_primary_email still produces the same successful schema check and digest (exit 0); the temporary change was restored. **Fix:** deterministically generate the composed Drizzle output, compare it to committed runtime schema and review migration effects. A lock of the abstract description alone is insufficient. ### Remaining issue scope Cursor consolidation is explicitly deferred in the PR; separate HMAC mechanics remain in domain search and audit pagination. Keep SKI-10 open and explicitly track the remaining phase. The PR's automated “closing out SKI-10” summary contradicts its own scope note. ## Validation and coverage 34 existing focused auth/email/observability/MCP audit tests in 14 files passed; auth package TypeScript passed. Two independent consumer regression assertions fail for the missing CSRF header and stale production token shape. Schema check passes on Node 22.22.1 and fails on 22.13.0; a temporary Drizzle-drift mutation passes the gate incorrectly. Database integration/security flows, full build/release gates, real-browser OTP/logout and deployed behavior remain unrun. Dependencies were reused, not installed cleanly; npx fetched Node 22.13.0 for the compatibility probe. CI at capture: security/reviewer checks mostly successful; Sourcery skipped. SonarCloud analysis was CANCELLED and its conversation comment reports a failed analysis. CodeRabbit also reports review-rate exhaustion. No hosted product build/test gate was shown in the fetched rollup; bot success does not establish release readiness. ## Review-surface triage 25 threads / 29 thread comments, 12 review bodies and 8 conversation comments captured with pagination complete. Production consumer and minimum-Node findings remain current; duplicates are grouped. The hard-coded 600-second UI TTL comment is not adopted as a current defect because the released send response lacks expiresInSeconds and the configured/default lifetime remains 600. This is current-head quality, not an original-submission/model benchmark. ## Findings ### F19-1 · P1 · Configure the native client's Skillplane CSRF cookie prefix The client at [client.ts:28](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/app/src/lib/auth/client.ts#L28) omits `cookiePrefix: "skillplane"` and [signOut:80](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/app/src/lib/auth/client.ts#L80) removes the old explicit CSRF header. The installed @authfn/client@0.2.0 infers the prefix only from a session cookie. AuthFn makes that cookie HttpOnly, so browser JavaScript sees `skillplane.csrf` but not the session cookie; the client falls back to `authfn.csrf` and omits x-authfn-csrf. The server's assertValidCsrf rejects authenticated sign-out without that header, leaving the session active. **Evidence:** actual app signOut wrapper + released client with realistic readable cookie and mocked fetch produced a null header instead of the sentinel. Cookie issuance and server validation were code-traced. No live logout was performed. **Fix:** configure the prefix explicitly and add a browser-realistic logout regression with the session cookie hidden. ### F19-2 · P2 · Migrate the production OTP verification consumer The new hook reads only [metadata.turnstileToken:18](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/packages/auth/src/otp-policy.ts#L18), but [verify-email-production.mjs:65](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/scripts/verify-email-production.mjs#L65) still sends a top-level token and requires accepted/expiresInSeconds. Native send returns challengeId/sent. The later verify request omits an explicit cookie session mode, but the released server defaults it to cookie; that omission is not a separate defect. **Impact:** the documented Turnstile-based production verification command cannot complete its OTP flow. **Evidence:** executing the actual script with a dummy recipient/token and mocked fetch captures no metadata.turnstileToken. Response and verification requirements were traced through the script and released OTP plugin. **Fix:** migrate request, native success checks and cookie-session verification together; test both stages with mocked external calls. ### F19-3 · P2 · Keep schema preflight executable on the declared minimum Node [check-authfn-schema.mjs:12](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/scripts/check-authfn-schema.mjs#L12) dynamically imports TypeScript from plain node. package.json declares Node \>=22.13.0, but this invocation fails there before checking the schema. **Evidence:** Node 22.13.0 exits 1 with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION for plugin-composition.ts. Node 22.22.1 exits 0 with the committed digest. **Fix:** use a supported loader/flag or built JavaScript across the declared range, or deliberately raise and document the minimum; verify the minimum version. ### F19-4 · P2 · Compare generated schema with the actual Drizzle schema [check-authfn-schema.mjs:31](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/scripts/check-authfn-schema.mjs#L31) hashes the AuthFn schema description but never generates or compares [the manually maintained Drizzle schema](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/0f55fd00d2bbb2c950139fed4cbda4406bc20b9e/packages/db/src/schema/authfn.ts). This does detect upstream/plugin description drift, but does not fulfill SKI-10's generated-schema parity requirement. **Evidence:** in a temporary copy, changing the actual users primary-email column to WRONG_primary_email still produces the same successful schema check and digest (exit 0); the temporary change was restored. **Fix:** deterministically generate the composed Drizzle output, compare it to committed runtime schema and review migration effects. A lock of the abstract description alone is insufficient. ### Remaining issue scope Cursor consolidation is explicitly deferred in the PR; separate HMAC mechanics remain in domain search and audit pagination. Keep SKI-10 open and explicitly track the remaining phase. The PR's automated “closing out SKI-10” summary contradicts its own scope note. ## Validation and coverage 34 existing focused auth/email/observability/MCP audit tests in 14 files passed; auth package TypeScript passed. Two independent consumer regression assertions fail for the missing CSRF header and stale production token shape. Schema check passes on Node 22.22.1 and fails on 22.13.0; a temporary Drizzle-drift mutation passes the gate incorrectly. Database integration/security flows, full build/release gates, real-browser OTP/logout and deployed behavior remain unrun. Dependencies were reused, not installed cleanly; npx fetched Node 22.13.0 for the compatibility probe. CI at capture: security/reviewer checks mostly successful; Sourcery skipped. SonarCloud analysis was CANCELLED and its conversation comment reports a failed analysis. CodeRabbit also reports review-rate exhaustion. No hosted product build/test gate was shown in the fetched rollup; bot success does not establish release readiness. ## Review-surface triage 25 threads / 29 thread comments, 12 review bodies and 8 conversation comments captured with pagination complete. Fencing epoch, raw provider cause, outage classification, schema plugin omission, idempotency freshness and stale status-field findings are fixed. Production consumer and minimum-Node findings remain current; duplicates are grouped. The hard-coded 600-second UI TTL comment is not adopted as a current defect because the released send response lacks expiresInSeconds and the configured/default lifetime remains 600. Incomplete error-body type guarding is unverified hardening without a malformed native producer. item.stdout: {"baseRefOid":"ad4308fa1f5bb3bfff043993ea162190d9375345","body":"Adds native skill composition so a published parent retains exact child versions and inherited verification obligations instead of relying on selectors embedded in Markdown. Format-v1 stays a leaf with unchanged canonical identity; format-v2 receives a server-generated transitive lock and closure digest at candidate creation, revalidated at publication without silently upgrading children. - Adds bounded DAG/semver resolution, normalized immutable dependency records, include/invoke plans, visibility checks, deprecation/revocation and explicit reviewable upgrades. - Adds independent verifier runs tied to closure, repository commit and environment, namespaced blocking/advisory claims, redacted evidence references, idempotent completion and 90-day retention. Blocking failed or unknown claims cannot pass. - Exposes composition authoring, dependency/closure changes and verification results through the app, HTTP and MCP. Includes DataFn and Linear composition examples, operational documentation, and regional/control migrations 0048–0051. Closes [SKI-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-3/support-native-skill-composition-dependency-resolution-and). Validation on the PR branch: - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` - `pnpm typecheck` — 32/32 tasks; Svelte 0 errors/warnings - `pnpm lint` - `pnpm test:unit` — 31/31 tasks - `pnpm build` — 18/18 tasks - 51 tests passed across 10 focused PostgreSQL integration and MCP/API/storage security suites, including composition, evidence gating, revoked-dependency replacement and retention after a workspace routing epoch change. Deploy readers and both database-role migrations before enabling v2 writers. `SKILL_COMPOSITION_WRITES_ENABLED=false` disables v2 writes while retaining reads. Evidence validation checks the attestation contract; the independent verifier remains responsible for the truth of referenced evidence. No deployment or browser visual QA was performed. `.conduct` notes are excluded, following the repository ignore policy. `.gitignore` is unchanged; local database, generated builds and test artifacts are already ignored. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds native skill composition (format-v2) so published parents keep exact child versions and inherited verification obligations at candidate creation, instead of relying on selectors embedded in Markdown. Closes [SKI-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-3/support-native-skill-composition-dependency-resolution-and). - Resolves bounded DAG/semver dependencies into immutable records with include/invoke plans, visibility checks, deprecation/revocation, and reviewable upgrades. - Adds independent verifier runs tied to closure, repository commit, and environment, with namespaced blocking/advisory claims and redacted evidence; blocking failed or unknown claims cannot pass. - Exposes composition authoring, dependency/closure changes, and verification results through the app, HTTP, and MCP. **Migration** - Deploy readers and both database-role migrations before enabling v2 writers. - `SKILL_COMPOSITION_WRITES_ENABLED=false` keeps v2 reads on while v2 writes stay off. - No deployment or browser visual QA was performed. item.stdout: {"baseRefOid":"ad4308fa1f5bb3bfff043993ea162190d9375345","body":"Implements [SKI-15](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-15/support-local-first-workspaces-and-resilient-agent-skill-projections): projects can create and manage skills locally without a cloud account, and installed agent skills retain a verified, self-contained snapshot when the cloud is unavailable. - Add `packages/local-runtime` with a standalone CLI/source installer, SQLite metadata and immutable bundles, local/cloud providers, protected account profiles, and explicit primary workspace plus ordered mounts. Local creation and amendments reuse shared domain bundle and validation rules. - Add Claude, Codex, and generic projections with atomic generation switches, crash recovery, ownership checks, trust approvals tied to exact digests, freshness policies, rollback, and safe uninstall. Live resolution verifies identity and matching resources before replacing embedded instructions. - Record local usage privately by default. Add authenticated, opt-in `skill_usage_report` uploads with durable event deduplication and reported/observed confidence distinctions; clarify analytics coverage in the dashboard. - Document setup, configuration, lifecycle operations, offline behavior, trust, and supported adapter boundaries. The runtime exposes setup APIs for a future desktop installer; this change does not add a native desktop application or signed public distribution. Validation on this PR branch, replayed cleanly onto current `main` (`ad4308f`): - 126 unit tests passed across local-runtime, domain, mcp-schema, and MCP, including a bundled CLI installation test. - 25 selected database integration/conformance tests passed across MCP read, resource routing, local-provider contract, and conformance suites. - Typechecks passed for the runtime, domain, schema, MCP, and app. Svelte reports one warning in unchanged `SkillEditor.svelte`. - Changed-file ESLint and Prettier checks, workspace boundaries, McpFn adoption, and diff whitespace checks passed. The full integration suite is not claimed green: the implementation checkout previously reproduced two caller-attribution expectation failures on its unchanged original base (`c650743`); the complete suite was not rerun on this updated base. Hosted CI and deployment are not part of this local verification. Local `.conduct` completion artifacts are excluded from this `main` PR. Existing ignore rules already cover generated outputs; `.gitignore` is unchanged. The original working checkout is preserved. --- ## Summary by cubic Implements [SKI-15](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-15/support-local-first-workspaces-and-resilient-agent-skill-projections). Previously, creating and managing skills required a cloud account and network; now projects can create and manage skills locally with the new `skillplane` client, and installed agent skills keep a verified snapshot when the cloud is unavailable. No native desktop app is included; the runtime exposes setup APIs for a future installer. **New Features** - Adds `packages/local-runtime` with a standalone CLI, SQLite metadata, immutable bundle storage, local/cloud providers, protected account profiles, and ordered workspace mounts. - Adds Claude, Codex, and generic projections with atomic switches, crash recovery, trust approvals tied to exact digests, freshness policies, rollback, and safe uninstall. - Local create and amend flows reuse the shared domain bundle and validation rules; live resolution verifies identity and resources before replacing embedded instructions. - Records local usage privately by default and adds the opt-in `skill_usage_report` MCP tool for deduplicated cloud uploads. - Dashboard analytics now distinguish observed cloud activity from client-reported events. **Validation** - Unit and integration tests pass for the new runtime and MCP tooling; the full integration suite is not claimed green. Written for commit cc34611f997c0eac391285aabce2c6912f88237c. Summary will update on new commits.     "text": "# PR quality analysis report template\n\nUse a compact chat verdict plus a dated, separately identifiable full analysis. Notion publication is the default unless explicitly disabled. Read `notion-publication.md` before publishing; use `integrations.md` when falling back to Composio.\n\n## Compact chat verdict\n\n**<rating>/10 — <assessment>; <readiness>.**\n\nBrief strengths and highest-impact actionable findings, with source links. State the exact reviewed head, focused test results, CI status and material limits. Link the verified Notion analysis and evidence (or the local artifact when publication is disabled/blocked). Name the reviewer harness/model when known; distinguish it from the implementation author.\n\nDo not copy old counts, ratings or attribution into a new analysis without verification. No findings means no actionable defects found within the recorded scope, not proof of defect-free code.\n\n## Analysis metadata\n\nInclude this block in every analysis, even if Notion has dedicated properties. Unavailable values are explicitly `unknown`; omit no distinction between author and reviewer.\n\n```yaml\nanalysis_id: <stable UUID for this fresh analysis; reused for publication retry>\nanalysis_type: <initial | same-head | new-head | targeted-follow-up>\nanalysis_status: <completed | partial | blocked>\nstarted_at: <ISO-8601 UTC>\ncompleted_at: <ISO-8601 UTC or unknown>\nprevious_analysis_id: <ID/link or none>\nrepository: <canonical repository URL>\npr_or_session: <PR URL or source session URL>\nreviewed_head: <full SHA>\nbase: <full SHA>\nmerge_base: <full SHA>\ncaptured_at: <ISO-8601 UTC>\nsource_snapshot: <requirement/document snapshot IDs or digests; limits explicit>\nscope: <reviewed and unreviewed surfaces>\nskill: <workspace/slug@published-version>\nrubric: <version or named dimensions/weights>\nreviewer:\n  harness_client: <name>\n  harness_version: <version or unknown>\n  provider: <provider or unknown>\n  model: <exact ID or unknown>\n  model_version: <version or unknown>\n  reasoning: <setting or unknown>\n  environment: <execution environment or unknown>\n  task_session: <ID/link or unknown>\n  attribution_source: <runtime metadata | user-supplied | other evidence | unknown>\n  attribution_confidence: <high | medium | low | unknown>\n  mixed_or_delegated: <material contributors/ranges or none>\nimplementation_author:\n  harness_model: <separate author attribution>\n  source_confidence: <evidence and confidence>\n  commit_range: <original/remediated range>\npublication:\n  destination: <Notion hub | local-only | blocked>\n  analysis_url: <verified URL or pending>\n  evidence_url: <verified URL or unavailable>\n```\n\nDo not guess the analyst model from the implementation badge, or the implementation model from the analyst's current runtime. An application name alone may not identify the underlying harness/version. Preserve requested-vs-confirmed model distinctions.\n\n## Issue overview\n\nOne issue overview, linked to implementation parents. Put the current comparison first:\n\n| Implementation | Latest analysis / reviewer | Reviewed SHA | Quality | Readiness | Strength | Main gap |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n\nFor a single PR, keep one row; do not invent comparators. Include source issue and acceptance/design links, recommendation, acceptance coverage, major differences and links to full analyses. Display same-head disagreement when it affects the recommendation. Use native Notion tables per the fetched Markdown specification.\n\n## Implementation parent and analysis history\n\nOne parent per repository/PR or non-PR session. Keep an analysis index:\n\n| Analysis ID / date | Reviewed head | Reviewer harness/model | Scope/status | Quality/verdict | Evidence |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n\nEach fresh assessment, including the same head, has its own analysis child page or existing database row. Retain earlier snapshots and metadata. Retrying publication uses the same ID and repairs its entry; a fresh assessment receives a new ID. Do not silently replace history or average scores. Identify the latest completed or explicitly adjudicated analysis on the parent.\n\n## Full analysis\n\n1. **Decision and scope:** concrete problem, implemented outcome, quality and readiness, source requirements and coverage limits.\n2. **Strengths and scoring:** weighted dimensions with rationale; average never overrides a blocker. Separate original code from author/third-party remediation.\n3. **Findings:** severity, trigger, expected/actual behavior, user impact, exact immutable file/line, evidence status, root cause, narrow complete fix and needed validation. Distinguish reproduced, code-traced, unverified, already fixed and duplicate.\n4. **Validation:** commands, reviewed SHA, runtime/dependency provenance, counts, failures, canceled/unrun checks and CI links. Classify changed-code, baseline, environment and unknown failures. Cover relevant public failure paths through artifact writing and publication/consumption, using mocks where live writes are not authorized.\n5. **Author process:** observed requirement → transcript decision → code consequence → missed verification, only where evidence exists. Label inferences and absent transcripts; include a concise author follow-up about a material deviation without presuming motive.\n6. **Analysis provenance and exposure:** reviewer metadata above, source/bot/transcript exposure, independent vs reused checks and any changes in reviewer model or scope. Do not claim blind/independent review when prior findings were available.\n7. **Evidence:** reproducible probes, input snapshots and immutable links. Record incomplete evidence and publication state honestly.\n\n## Evidence bundle\n\nProvide minimal runnable probe source and commands, fixtures/setup, runtime and reused/installed dependencies, expected-vs-actual behavior, output/exit status and relevant CI/source links. Label fixture repository SHAs separately from the PR head. Redact secrets and unrelated private material. Include source scripts alongside outputs; outputs alone may be insufficient to reproduce the result.\n\nFull transcripts are copied only when requested or otherwise authorized; default review publication includes pertinent excerpts/source links and explicit availability. Preserve timestamps/ranges and distinguish excerpts from complete transcripts. Place long evidence in child pages/attachments. Replace local-only links before publication and verify the uploaded content.\n\n## Publication verification\n\nPublish to the intended hub unless explicitly disabled; no redundant authorization prompt. Query for existing issue/PR/analysis identities. Read schemas and preserve existing structure. Update properties separately from content where required. Read back analysis ID, reviewer metadata, findings including the final finding, score/verdict, reviewed SHA, evidence content/links, issue relations and history. State partial writes and blockers accurately; retry with the same analysis ID.\n\nKeep author/model aggregates in their separate scorecard. Multiple analyses of one PR do not create additional independent author samples. Preserve analysis-level disagreements rather than manufacturing a consensus or leaderboard.\n",

    "text": "# Default Notion publication and multiple analyses\n\nPublish the finished review to the intended Notion QA hub unless the user explicitly opts out. The workflow grants this reporting default; do not add a confirmation gate merely because Notion is external. Respect an explicit local-only/chat-only/no-external-writes instruction. Confirm the intended workspace/destination from current connection and existing context; ambiguity requires destination clarification, not a new permission question. Do not broaden sharing, create a public site or modify unrelated pages.\n\n## Reuse identity, preserve analysis history\n\n- One issue overview per canonical repository/issue context; one implementation parent per repository/PR (or non-PR session).\n- One analysis record/child page per fresh assessment, even at the same head and by the same reviewer. Generate `analysis_id` once (UUID is suitable), keep it in the report and evidence, and preserve it across upload retries/corrections to that analysis.\n- A new assessment has a new analysis ID, timestamps, reviewer metadata, findings, score, validation and evidence. Link `previous_analysis_id` / `supersedes_analysis_id` when applicable without deleting the prior result. A changed head is not required for a new analysis.\n- Prefer the hub's existing analysis-history database when present. If the schema has only one Implementation Review per PR, keep that parent and create analysis child pages with an index table. Do not create duplicate PR parents or remodel unrelated databases. For legacy parents containing a single review, preserve the existing content as historical and append/index the new analysis; do not retroactively invent unknown reviewer metadata.\n- Use `(repository, PR/session, analysis_id)` for publication deduplication. A retry updates the matching record. Never deduplicate distinct analyses solely by head SHA, model or date.\n- The issue overview and PR parent can display the latest completed analysis, with its analysis ID, timestamp, reviewer and reviewed SHA. A partial or blocked new analysis does not silently replace a prior completed verdict. Same-head disagreements remain visible; do not merge findings or average scores without adjudication.\n\n## Required analysis metadata\n\nSeparate **implementation author** from **analysis performer** in both labels and data. Record:\n\n- Analysis ID; start/completion timestamps; status; scope; reason/type (initial, same-head independent assessment, new-head re-review, targeted follow-up); prior analysis link when relevant.\n- Repository/PR/session; reviewed head, base and merge base; capture/freshness time; requirement/source snapshot identities; skill slug, published version and report/rubric version.\n- Reviewer harness/client and version, provider, exact model/version, reasoning setting, execution environment, task/session ID/link; source and confidence for this attribution. Record mixed turns or delegated reviewers where material. Use explicit `unknown` rather than inferring identity from the current app label or implementation author.\n- Author harness/model provenance separately, with the original-vs-remediated commit range and evidence/confidence.\n- Findings, score dimensions/verdict, commands/probes, dependency environment, coverage gaps and publication state.\n\nDo not repurpose an existing Author Harness/Model column as reviewer metadata. Put analysis metadata in dedicated properties if the schema supports them and always in the analysis body. If schema changes are unnecessary, the child-page body and index are sufficient.\n\n## Publication sequence\n\n1. Fetch connection identity, hub, schemas and current issue/PR entries. Query all necessary pages to establish duplicates/history. Fetch the enhanced Markdown spec when required by the tool. Use direct Notion first, then Composio on access failure; reuse schemas and IDs throughout.\n2. Prepare a concise issue overview, full analysis, and an evidence child page/bundle. Keep comparison first, detailed findings below, transcripts behind links. Never label missing transcripts as copied or verified.\n3. Publish the analysis and evidence using the stable analysis ID. Include runnable minimal probe scripts/commands, fixtures/setup, runtime/dependencies, stdout/stderr and exit statuses, expected-vs-actual behavior, immutable code/source links, and redaction notes. Label fixture SHAs separately from reviewed PR SHAs. Use mocks for unapproved external writes and dummy secrets for credential probes.\n4. Replace local filesystem links with uploaded files or Notion evidence references. Do not publish broken `/tmp/...` links. If a full log or script cannot be uploaded, preserve the minimal reproducible recipe and explicitly list the unavailable evidence; do not call an output-only dump a complete reproduction bundle.\n5. Update the parent/index, issue relations and hub summary narrowly, preserving unrelated wording and historical analyses. Compute counts from actual records: issue count, unique implementation count and analysis count are different. Do not inflate author scorecard sample counts when adding another analysis of the same PR.\n6. Use **separate `update_properties` and `update_content` operations** where the connector treats them separately. In the observed direct connector, `update_content` returned success while ignoring accompanying properties. Do not assume properties applied because content did. Inspect current schemas/help for Composio equivalents instead of copying direct-tool arguments.\n7. Read back every material write: full finding set and tail, native tables, reviewer/author metadata, score/verdict, SHA, analysis ID, evidence URLs, both directions of relations and retained history. Verify evidence content, not just the existence of a child page. Check truncation/unknown blocks and pagination. Repair partial property/link writes without duplicating pages.\n8. Final response: verified analysis URL, issue overview if useful, and concise publication limitations. If publication remains blocked after fallback, say what succeeded and what remains, and keep the same analysis ID for continuation.\n\n## Scorecards\n\nKeep author-implementation quality and reviewer-analysis quality separate. Multiple reviewers assessing one PR are paired analyses of one implementation, not independent author samples. Preserve per-analysis scores and disagreements; choose a latest/adjudicated summary explicitly and retain the decision trail. Update aggregate counts only when the existing rubric and denominator justify it. Publishing a review does not authorize inventing a model leaderboard.\n",
