If the ephemeral platform cannot register prompts or commands dynamically from MCP, Skillplane provides retrieval and use but does not claim native slash commands.\\n\\n## Security and privacy\\n\\n* Store account credentials only in an operating-system credential store or equivalent protected secret service.\\n* Never embed credentials in projections or project configuration.\\n* Qualify workspace and skill identity to prevent cross-account slug confusion.\\n* Validate bundle paths against traversal and symlink escape.\\n* Enforce compressed and expanded size limits, file-count limits, and permitted media types.\\n* Treat skill content and scripts as untrusted until covered by the active trust policy.\\n* Sign or digest projection manifests so divergence and local edits are detectable.\\n* Keep local analytics local by default unless consent or organization policy authorizes upload.\\n* Avoid identifying a human from an agent invocation unless the authenticated transport already establishes that identity.\\n\\n## Reliability and recovery\\n\\n* Projection writes are journaled, idempotent, and atomic per target.\\n* Existing user-owned files are never silently overwritten.\\n* Interrupted sync resumes or rolls back from the mutation journal.\\n* Cloud outages cannot corrupt local workspace authority.\\n* Authentication expiry affects cloud resolution but not permitted local fallback.\\n* A failed association between a projection and state record is detected during the next health check.\\n* `skillplane doctor` reports missing CLI integration, stale projections, divergent files, credential failures, unresolved collisions, and pending trust approvals.\\n\\n## Migration and compatibility\\n\\n1. Inventory existing user-managed and Skillplane-managed agent skill directories.\\n2. Introduce projection ownership manifests without adopting unrelated files.\\n3. Import existing Skillplane projections as pinned snapshots where provenance can be verified.\\n4. Allow users to choose resilient or strict-live policy before enabling runtime checks.\\n5. Preserve static export as a fallback for unsupported agent hosts.\\n6. Add cloud profiles without converting local workspaces automatically.\\n\\nRollback removes only files proven to be owned by the selected projection and restores the previous owned projection tree. It does not delete local workspace data or unrelated agent skills.\\n\\n## Proposed delivery sequence\\n\\n### Phase 1: contracts and capability model\\n\\nDefine workspace providers, project contexts, qualified selectors, projection adapter capabilities, version/offline policies, trust envelopes, and analytics semantics.\\n\\n### Phase 2: embedded local workspace\\n\\nImplement local immutable skill/version operations, content storage, credential-independent local setup, and explicit import/export.\\n\\n### Phase 3: global CLI and projections\\n\\nImplement account profiles, primary-plus-mount routing, atomic projection sync, ownership manifests, collision handling, and diagnostics.\\n\\n### Phase 4: resilient runtime resolution\\n\\nAdd freshness checks, exact digest confirmation, cached fallback, trust-policy gating, and target-specific deterministic integrations where supported.\\n\\n### Phase 5: shared creation and amendments\\n\\nExpose the common domain operations through local CLI/desktop and cloud MCP, retaining immutable exact-base semantics.\\n\\n### Phase 6: analytics and privacy controls\\n\\nAdd local event queues, cloud ingestion, delivery-mode/confidence reporting, opt-in controls, and dashboards that disclose coverage.\\n\\n### Phase 7: desktop and nontechnical onboarding\\n\\nBuild the desktop wizard and initialization-skill flow on the same setup engine; add one-command bootstrap packaging and recovery UX.\\n\\n## Validation strategy\\n\\n* Contract tests run against both local and cloud workspace providers.\\n* Projection golden tests cover every supported target's paths, metadata, and content.\\n* Fault injection covers interruption before write, during swap, and before state commit.\\n* Security tests cover traversal, symlink escape, digest mismatch, decompression limits, executable scripts, and permission expansion.\\n* Multi-account tests cover identical slugs, expired credentials, profile switching, and explicit write destinations.\\n* Offline tests cover cached and strict failure policies.\\n* Analytics tests verify event boundaries, local queue replay, idempotency, and disclosed coverage.\\n* Ephemeral MCP tests prove operation without local files and reject unauthorized cross-workspace access.\\n* User-flow tests cover one-command installation, desktop setup, uninstall ownership, and recovery.\\n\\n## Risks and tradeoffs\\n\\n* Inline embedded content maximizes compatibility but always consumes context and can coexist with newer live output.\\n* Sibling fallback content reduces normal context but depends on the host's ability to read supporting files.\\n* Behavioral freshness instructions can be skipped by an agent; deterministic injection is host-specific.\\n* Following latest content reduces reproducibility; pinned mode reduces amendment immediacy.\\n* Rich analytics can conflict with local privacy expectations if defaults are not conservative.\\n* Supporting many agent adapters may create a long-lived compatibility burden.\\n* A broad first release risks coupling local storage, sync, desktop, analytics, and MCP changes; phased contracts are essential.\\n\\n## Open questions\\n\\n* Confirm the embedded storage technology and backup/export format.\\n* Choose the default fallback layout: inline body or sibling snapshot.\\n* Define the first supported agent-adapter matrix and exact guarantees.\\n* Decide whether live resolution updates the projection synchronously, asynchronously, or only on explicit sync.\\n* Define organization-level controls over offline fallback and analytics upload.\\n* Select collision UX and stable alias rules.\\n* Determine whether local-to-cloud replication remains permanently explicit or becomes a later opt-in capability.\",\"icon\":null,\"color\":null,\"url\":\"https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-15-support-local-first-workspaces-9f8209e784e5\",\"slugId\":\"9f8209e784e5\",\"createdAt\":\"2026-08-30T12:31:34.049Z\",\"updatedAt\":\"2026-08-30T12:31:34.663Z\",\"archivedAt\":null,\"creator\":{\"id\":\"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a\",\"name\":\"Aravind\"},\"updatedBy\":{\"id\":\"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a\",\"name\":\"Aravind\"},\"project\":null,\"initiative\":null,\"team\":null,\"issue\":{\"id\":\"SKI-15\",\"title\":\"Support local-first workspaces and resilient agent skill projections\"}}"}]}}}
{"status":"fulfilled","value":{"name":"ski15-ideation","r":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"id\":\"568038ca-a020-45ef-a3f2-d77f8cd2f681\",\"title\":\"Ideation & Product Rationale — SKI-15: Support local-first workspaces and resilient agent skill projections\",\"content\":\"**Backlog issue:** [SKI-15 — Support local-first workspaces and resilient agent skill projections](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-15/support-local-first-workspaces-and-resilient-agent-skill-projections>)\\n\\n## Context and motivating problem\\n\\nSkillplane needs an onboarding and runtime model that is useful beyond the managed cloud. The discussion started from a desired one-command initialization experience that can eventually install the CLI and desktop app, while also serving nontechnical users through an agent-driven initialization skill.\\n\\nThe scope then expanded to the operating model required underneath that onboarding:\\n\\n* use Skillplane locally without Skillplane managed cloud;\\n* expose Skillplane skills through agent-recognized filesystem directories and native slash commands;\\n* combine local and cloud workspaces, including multiple cloud accounts;\\n* understand how often skills are used and which agent used them;\\n* preserve skill creation and amendment flows currently exposed through MCP;\\n* support ephemeral cloud agents that have MCP but no persistent local filesystem;\\n* retain a usable fallback when the CLI, MCP, authentication, or network is unavailable.\\n\\nThe central product tension is freshness and observability versus resilience. A static skill projection keeps working but can become stale and invisible to analytics. A thin runtime launcher can resolve the latest instructions and record invocation, but it creates a hard runtime dependency. A hybrid projection attempts to preserve both properties honestly.\\n\\n## Target users and stakeholders\\n\\n### Individual local user\\n\\nWants Skillplane on one machine without creating or depending on a managed-cloud account. Expects a straightforward installer, offline operation, and native skills inside familiar agents.\\n\\n### Nontechnical user\\n\\nWants the desktop app or an initialization skill to discover agents, configure directories, and explain account/workspace choices without requiring shell expertise.\\n\\n### Developer using several agents\\n\\nWants the same Skillplane catalog available in Claude, Codex, Cursor, or other supported hosts while retaining host-specific discovery and invocation behavior.\\n\\n### Multi-account professional\\n\\nHas personal and work cloud accounts plus local project workspaces. Needs unambiguous resolution, safe credential storage, and a clear destination for new skills and amendments.\\n\\n### Workspace administrator\\n\\nWants controlled updates, provenance, permission review, useful adoption analytics, and no silent expansion of a skill's trust envelope.\\n\\n### Ephemeral cloud agent\\n\\nHas no durable filesystem or desktop application. It must discover, retrieve, create, and amend authorized skills through MCP alone.\\n\\n## Desired user journeys\\n\\n### First-time initialization\\n\\n1. The user installs Skillplane through a one-command bootstrap or desktop installer.\\n2. Setup discovers supported agents and their recognized skill directories.\\n3. The user can start with a local workspace, sign into one or more cloud accounts, or do both.\\n4. Setup creates an explicit project context with one primary write workspace and optional mounted skill sources.\\n5. Skillplane projects selected skills and reports exactly what it created.\\n\\n### Native skill invocation\\n\\n1. The user invokes a projected skill through an agent's native command or automatic discovery.\\n2. The projection prefers Skillplane CLI resolution, or Skillplane MCP when that is the available transport.\\n3. Live resolution checks the bundled version and digest, records an observed invocation, and returns newer permitted instructions only when needed.\\n4. If neither transport is available, the agent uses the embedded snapshot and discloses its version and unverified freshness.\\n5. The agent uses exactly one instruction source rather than merging live and fallback instructions.\\n\\n### Multiple accounts and workspaces\\n\\n1. The user signs into named profiles such as work and personal; credentials remain in the operating-system credential store.\\n2. A project chooses one primary workspace for writes and ordered mounts for additional skills.\\n3. Skill references remain qualified internally so identical slugs do not resolve accidentally across accounts.\\n4. Creation and amendments always have an explicit write destination.\\n\\n### Ephemeral MCP-only agent\\n\\n1. The environment receives a Skillplane MCP endpoint and short-lived scoped credentials.\\n2. The agent discovers and retrieves skills without installing filesystem projections.\\n3. Retrieval and mutation events are observed by the service.\\n4. Native slash commands are available only if the host separately supports dynamic MCP prompts or commands; Skillplane does not claim this universally.\\n\\n## Ideas discussed\\n\\n### Proposal: one canonical setup engine\\n\\nThe CLI command, desktop wizard, bootstrap script, and initialization skill should call the same idempotent setup operations. The public installation surface can be simple while avoiding duplicated configuration logic.\\n\\n### Proposal: local and cloud as workspace providers\\n\\nLocal storage and Skillplane Cloud should expose the same domain capabilities through different providers. CLI, desktop, API, and MCP are transports into those capabilities rather than separate implementations.\\n\\n### Proposal: primary workspace plus mounts\\n\\nA project should have exactly one primary write workspace and zero or more mounted sources. This supports simultaneous local and multi-account cloud access without making the destination of skill creation or amendments ambiguous.\\n\\n### Preferred direction under discussion: resilient projections\\n\\nProjected skills remain self-contained and contain a versioned fallback snapshot. Their first instruction asks the agent to retrieve or verify the skill through the global Skillplane CLI or MCP when available, then use the embedded content only as fallback. No resolver executable is copied into each skill folder.\\n\\n### Proposal: policy modes\\n\\n* `resilient`: prefer live resolution and fall back to the packaged snapshot;\\n* `strict-live`: require a successful freshness check and observed invocation;\\n* `pinned`: use an exact immutable packaged version.\\n\\n### Proposal: honest analytics\\n\\nSkillplane should distinguish projection/install, live retrieval or invocation, downstream Skillplane tool activity, reported completion, and independently verified success. Embedded use without CLI or MCP contact is unobservable and must not be presented as complete usage.\\n\\n## Alternatives and tradeoffs\\n\\n### Static projection only\\n\\nPros: portable, inspectable, offline, low runtime complexity. Cons: stale content, delayed amendments, no direct invocation analytics, and repeated sync work.\\n\\n### Thin runtime launcher only\\n\\nPros: latest policy enforcement, single authoritative body, smaller projection, stronger observed analytics. Cons: CLI/MCP/auth/network failures can make the native skill unusable, which is unfriendly for local and nontechnical users.\\n\\n### Agent hooks\\n\\nPros: can observe lifecycle events in supported hosts. Cons: host-specific, operationally invasive, and unavailable in many ephemeral or generic agent environments. The discussion favored projection-driven resolution as the primary mechanism rather than making hooks mandatory.\\n\\n### Resolver executable in every skill directory\\n\\nPros: can normalize command-missing and fallback behavior. Cons: duplicates runtime logic, complicates trust and updates, and turns each projection into a mini application. The discussion explicitly simplified this to one global CLI plus self-contained projected skills.\\n\\n### Automatic bidirectional local/cloud synchronization\\n\\nPros: seamless movement across devices and authorities. Cons: introduces conflict resolution, offline mutation reconciliation, authorization semantics, and difficult failure modes. The current proposal keeps authorities separate and uses explicit publish/import operations initially.\\n\\n## Desired outcomes and success measures\\n\\n* A local-only user can initialize and use Skillplane without a cloud account.\\n* A nontechnical user can complete setup without manually editing agent configuration files.\\n* Supported agents discover projected skills in their native locations.\\n* The common case confirms the embedded version without duplicating the whole skill body in context.\\n* Accepted amendments become available through the declared freshness policy.\\n* No projection update overwrites unrelated user content.\\n* Analytics dashboards label observed scope and delivery mode instead of implying complete totals.\\n* Ephemeral MCP-only agents have the same authorized domain operations even though they lack filesystem projection.\\n* Permission-expanding updates require explicit approval.\\n\\n## Product, UX, and operational considerations\\n\\n* Setup must explain local-only, connected, and MCP-only modes in user language.\\n* Account and workspace selectors should use friendly aliases while preserving qualified internal identity.\\n* A stale fallback should display its exact version and last synchronization time.\\n* Errors should distinguish CLI unavailable, authentication expired, cloud unreachable, policy-blocked update, and corrupt projection.\\n* Projection conflicts should be surfaced before writes and resolved through aliases, namespaces, or explicit precedence.\\n* The desktop app can later visualize sources, projection health, pending trust approvals, and locally queued analytics.\\n\\n## Goals\\n\\n* Deliver a coherent local-first and connected Skillplane experience.\\n* Make native agent skill discovery resilient.\\n* Preserve current cloud MCP capabilities.\\n* Establish truthful freshness, trust, and analytics semantics.\\n\\n## Non-goals\\n\\n* Guarantee universal slash-command behavior across all agents.\\n* Guarantee observation of completely disconnected fallback usage.\\n* Implement automatic local/cloud replication in the first iteration.\\n* Approve implementation, staffing, dates, or deployment through this backlog item.\\n\\n## Assumptions\\n\\n* **Assumption:** The CLI will be installed for the normal local experience even though projections must retain a fallback.\\n* **Assumption:** Agent-specific projection adapters are required because no universal skill directory or execution behavior exists.\\n* **Assumption:** Local analytics should remain local unless the user or organization explicitly enables upload.\\n\\n## Open questions\\n\\n* Is SQLite plus filesystem content storage the correct first embedded local provider?\\n* Should the fallback body live inline in `SKILL.md` for maximum compatibility or in a sibling snapshot to reduce context and conflict risk?\\n* Which hosts can guarantee a pre-model freshness command, and which can only receive best-effort instructions?\\n* What is the default policy for team-owned skills when cloud freshness cannot be confirmed?\\n* How should same-name skills from mounted sources appear as slash commands?\\n* Should accepted live content rewrite the projection immediately or only during the next explicit sync?\\n\\n## Acceptance criteria\\n\\nThe blocking acceptance criteria are maintained on <issue id=\\\"bd8d61d1-715a-4fea-8c0d-0f092c0a6d98\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-15/support-local-first-workspaces-and-resilient-agent-skill-projections\\\">SKI-15</issue>. Product acceptance additionally requires clear mode selection, disclosed degraded behavior, and no misleading claims about freshness, analytics completeness, or native host capabilities.\",\"icon\":null,\"color\":null,\"url\":\"https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-15-support-local-first-workspaces-709fa4e06ec4\",\"slugId\":\"709fa4e06ec4\",\"createdAt\":\"2026-08-30T12:31:31.656Z\",\"updatedAt\":\"2026-08-30T12:31:32.400Z\",\"archivedAt\":null,\"creator\":{\"id\":\"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a\",\"name\":\"Aravind\"},\"updatedBy\":{\"id\":\"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a\",\"name\":\"Aravind\"},\"project\":null,\"initiative\":null,\"team\":null,\"issue\":{\"id\":\"SKI-15\",\"title\":\"Support local-first workspaces and resilient agent skill projections\"}}"}]}}}

skill composition, dependency resolution, and verification modules\",\"content\":\"# Architecture & Delivery Plan\\n\\n**Linear issue:** [SKI-3 — Support native skill composition, dependency resolution, and verification modules](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-3/support-native-skill-composition-dependency-resolution-and>)\\n\\n## Current-state constraints\\n\\nSkillplane currently has strong leaf-skill primitives:\\n\\n* strict format-v1 skill.json validation with one SKILL.md execution entrypoint;\\n* bounded canonical ZIP validation and deterministic content digests;\\n* immutable skill versions stored as content-addressed bundles;\\n* version rows, per-file descriptors, semantic publication, and amendment review;\\n* stale-base and concurrent-publication protection;\\n* exact version and digest retrieval through MCP;\\n* workspace visibility and authorization on the selected root skill.\\n\\nComposition and verification are not modeled:\\n\\n* dependencies exist only if prose tells an agent to retrieve another skill;\\n* root bundle path rules do not provide a verification module root;\\n* persistence has no version-to-version dependency edges or closure identity;\\n* publication validates only the candidate root bundle and base version;\\n* retrieval returns one root instruction document rather than a dependency DAG;\\n* the editor changes SKILL.md but has no dependency or verification authoring UI;\\n* verification results are not attached to a skill closure or implementation revision.\\n\\n## Proposed architecture\\n\\n### Bundle format v2\\n\\nExtend skill.json while retaining format v1 as a valid leaf format.\\n\\nExample authored declaration:\\n\\n```\\n{\\n  \\\"formatVersion\\\": 2,\\n  \\\"entrypoints\\\": {\\n    \\\"execute\\\": \\\"SKILL.md\\\",\\n    \\\"verify\\\": \\\"verification/VERIFY.md\\\"\\n  },\\n  \\\"dependencies\\\": [\\n    {\\n      \\\"alias\\\": \\\"linear\\\",\\n      \\\"workspace\\\": \\\"21n\\\",\\n      \\\"skill\\\": \\\"create-and-associate-linear-issue\\\",\\n      \\\"version\\\": \\\"^1.0.0\\\",\\n      \\\"scope\\\": \\\"execution\\\",\\n      \\\"mode\\\": \\\"invoke\\\"\\n    }\\n  ],\\n  \\\"verification\\\": {\\n    \\\"claims\\\": \\\"verification/claims.json\\\",\\n    \\\"blocking\\\": true\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nAdd supported bundle roots for verification modules and a server-generated skill.lock.json. The server must ignore any caller-supplied lock and regenerate it.\\n\\n### Dependency semantics\\n\\nEach direct dependency contains:\\n\\n* stable alias;\\n* workspace and skill selector;\\n* semantic version constraint;\\n* scope: execution, verification, or both;\\n* mode: include or invoke;\\n* optional deterministic order;\\n* required flag, defaulting to true.\\n\\nInclude activates the child's module in the resolved plan. Invoke exposes the child as a named operation with a handoff boundary. Do not merge files or instructions by filename.\\n\\n### Candidate-time resolver\\n\\nDuring skill creation or candidate generation:\\n\\n 1. Parse and validate the authored v2 manifest.\\n 2. Resolve every direct constraint to an authorized published version.\\n 3. Recursively resolve transitive dependencies.\\n 4. Build a topologically ordered DAG.\\n 5. Reject cycles, conflicting constraints, duplicate aliases, revoked or inaccessible nodes, and visibility widening.\\n 6. Enforce maximum depth, direct dependencies, total closure nodes, and expanded bytes.\\n 7. Generate an exact lock containing version IDs, semantic versions, digests, modes, scopes, order, and transitive closure digests.\\n 8. Canonicalize the root bundle including the generated lock.\\n 9. Store normalized dependency edges with the candidate.\\n10. Present the complete closure diff for review.\\n\\nAt publication, revalidate that every locked node remains published and authorized. Do not silently select a newer version. If the locked closure is invalid, publication fails with a typed conflict.\\n\\n### Composition identity\\n\\nAdd dependencyClosureDigest to each version.\\n\\nCompute it from:\\n\\n* root bundle digest;\\n* ordered normalized direct edges;\\n* exact child version IDs and digests;\\n* each child's closure digest;\\n* composition scope and mode.\\n\\nThe root version ID plus closure digest identifies the logical composite.\\n\\n## Data model\\n\\n### skill_version_dependencies\\n\\nSuggested columns:\\n\\n* parent_version_id;\\n* alias;\\n* ordinal;\\n* scope;\\n* mode;\\n* requested_constraint;\\n* child_workspace_id;\\n* child_skill_id;\\n* resolved_version_id;\\n* resolved_semantic_version;\\n* resolved_digest;\\n* child_closure_digest;\\n* created_at.\\n\\nConstraints should enforce unique parent aliases and order, exact resolved published versions, and tenant-safe references.\\n\\n### skill_versions additions\\n\\n* format_version;\\n* dependency_closure_digest;\\n* direct_dependency_count;\\n* transitive_dependency_count;\\n* verification_claim_count.\\n\\n### Verification specification\\n\\nParse verification/claims.json into immutable normalized records or a validated JSON representation attached to the version.\\n\\nClaim fields:\\n\\n* id;\\n* statement;\\n* severity: blocking or advisory;\\n* scope;\\n* required evidence types;\\n* prohibited bypasses;\\n* pass, fail, and unknown rules;\\n* optional verifier procedure reference;\\n* optional waiver policy.\\n\\n### Verification runs and results\\n\\nskill_verification_runs:\\n\\n* root skill version;\\n* closure digest;\\n* target repository and commit;\\n* environment;\\n* verifier principal and declared agent/model;\\n* status;\\n* started and completed timestamps;\\n* evidence manifest digest.\\n\\nskill_verification_claim_results:\\n\\n* run;\\n* namespaced claim ID;\\n* originating skill version;\\n* pass, fail, or unknown;\\n* explanation;\\n* evidence references and digests;\\n* waiver reference when applicable.\\n\\nLarge evidence should remain in private content-addressed storage with bounded metadata in Postgres.\\n\\n## MCP and API surfaces\\n\\n### skill_resolve\\n\\nInput:\\n\\n* exact root selector/version;\\n* purpose: execute or verify;\\n* optional context selector;\\n* expansion limit preferences bounded by server policy.\\n\\nOutput:\\n\\n* root version and closure digest;\\n* ordered dependency DAG;\\n* namespaced execution modules;\\n* invocation contracts;\\n* inherited verification claims;\\n* deprecations and warnings;\\n* authorized asset descriptors.\\n\\n### skill_retrieve compatibility\\n\\nExisting skill_retrieve remains leaf-compatible. It may add expandDependencies for capable clients, but a dedicated skill_resolve makes the semantic difference clearer.\\n\\nFor legacy clients, the server may return deterministic combinedInstructions with explicit module boundaries. The structured plan remains canonical.\\n\\n### Verification tools\\n\\nAdd:\\n\\n* skill_verification_plan_get;\\n* skill_verification_run_start;\\n* skill_verification_evidence_add;\\n* skill_verification_run_complete;\\n* skill_verification_run_get.\\n\\nAll mutations require idempotency and audit attribution.\\n\\n## Verification composition\\n\\n* Namespaced claim identity is originating version plus claim ID.\\n* The verification closure is the union of all applicable child claims.\\n* Parents may add or strengthen claims.\\n* Parents cannot remove or weaken blocking child claims without an explicit reviewed waiver.\\n* Blocking failed or unknown claims prevent a passing run.\\n* Advisory unknown claims remain visible but do not block.\\n* Verification instructions are retrieved independently from execution instructions.\\n\\n## DataFn verification example\\n\\nThe Use DataFn skill should contain blocking claims such as:\\n\\n### datafn.read-surfaces\\n\\nEvery application read surface must be inventoried and traced through an approved DataFn client or adapter.\\n\\nRequired evidence:\\n\\n* generated or reviewed read-surface inventory;\\n* static dependency or call-path trace;\\n* representative runtime traces;\\n* integration tests for key reads.\\n\\n### datafn.mutations\\n\\nEvery application mutation must route through approved DataFn mutation APIs.\\n\\nRequired evidence:\\n\\n* mutation inventory;\\n* static bypass scan;\\n* representative successful and failing mutation tests;\\n* authorization and tenant-isolation evidence.\\n\\n### datafn.no-bypass\\n\\nDirect database, storage, or parallel API access outside explicitly approved adapter boundaries is prohibited.\\n\\nInstalling a package, generating schemas, mounting an unused endpoint, or importing a client is not evidence of compliance. Any unaccounted surface yields unknown, which is blocking.\\n\\n## Authorization and lifecycle\\n\\n* Authorize every closure node at candidate creation, publication, and retrieval.\\n* A public root may only include public dependencies.\\n* Workspace composites may include workspace-visible dependencies in the same authorized workspace.\\n* MVP should restrict private cross-workspace dependencies.\\n* Separate deprecated from revoked. Deprecated pinned versions remain retrievable with warnings; revoked dependencies fail closed.\\n* Root mutation authority never expands child authority or vice versa.\\n* Verification evidence follows the narrowest applicable visibility and retention policy.\\n\\n## Reliability and observability\\n\\nEmit structured events for:\\n\\n* resolution started/completed/failed;\\n* cycle and constraint conflict;\\n* authorization or visibility failure;\\n* publication revalidation failure;\\n* closure retrieval latency and size;\\n* verification run and claim outcomes;\\n* waiver creation and use;\\n* dependency revocation impact.\\n\\nExpose dependency path details in typed errors while redacting inaccessible resource identity.\\n\\nCache resolved immutable closures by closure digest. Never cache authorization decisions beyond their safe validity window.\\n\\n## Migration and backward compatibility\\n\\n* Format-v1 skills have an empty dependency graph and no verification plan.\\n* Existing version digests and retrieval behavior do not change.\\n* Introduce new nullable columns and new tables through a forward migration.\\n* Backfill format_version = 1 and closure digest derived from the root digest.\\n* Deploy readers before writers.\\n* Keep old MCP schemas operational while new tools roll out.\\n* No bulk rewrite of historical bundles is required.\\n\\n## Delivery phases\\n\\n### Phase 1: dependency foundation\\n\\n* v2 schemas and bundle paths;\\n* resolver and bounds;\\n* generated lock;\\n* normalized edges and closure digest;\\n* publication revalidation;\\n* unit, integration, security, and concurrency tests.\\n\\n### Phase 2: retrieval and authoring\\n\\n* skill_resolve MCP/API;\\n* composite editor;\\n* graph and closure diff;\\n* upgrade-available candidates;\\n* legacy combined-instructions adapter.\\n\\n### Phase 3: verification modules\\n\\n* verifier entrypoint and claims schema;\\n* verification-plan composition;\\n* runs, evidence, attestations, and audit;\\n* executor/verifier separation;\\n* DataFn reference skill and negative bypass tests.\\n\\n### Phase 4: governance and ecosystem\\n\\n* deprecation/revocation impact analysis;\\n* dependency upgrade automation;\\n* reusable verification-only skills;\\n* policy-based publication and verification gates;\\n* analytics and operational dashboards.\\n\\n## Validation and rollout\\n\\n* Golden resolver fixtures for direct, diamond, deep, conflicting, and cyclic graphs.\\n* Cross-workspace authorization and visibility tests.\\n* Concurrent child publication and parent approval tests.\\n* Closure-digest determinism across runtimes.\\n* Retrieval tests proving identical output for a pinned composite.\\n* Negative verification fixtures where a dependency is scaffolded but bypassed.\\n* Production canary using the existing Issue Fix/Add to Backlog shared Linear dependency.\\n* Company-stack canary combining UI, auth, and data skills.\\n* Rollback disables v2 writes while retaining read compatibility for already published v2 bundles.\\n\\n## Risks and tradeoffs\\n\\n* Graph resolution increases publication and retrieval complexity.\\n* Flattened legacy output may still create natural-language conflicts; structured modules reduce but do not eliminate them.\\n* Revocation semantics can conflict with reproducibility and require explicit product policy.\\n* Verification quality depends on claim quality and evidence access.\\n* Overly broad verification can be expensive; claim scope and representative runtime evidence must be explicit.\\n* Cross-workspace dependency authorization is substantially harder than same-workspace composition.\\n\\n## Open questions\\n\\nOpen product questions are tracked in [SKI-3](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-3/support-native-skill-composition-dependency-resolution-and>). Decisions should be recorded there before implementation changes the persistence or public MCP contract.\",\"icon\":null,\"color\":null,\"url\":\"https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-3-support-native-skill-composition-7187021da718\",\"slugId\":\"7187021da718\",\"createdAt\":\"2026-08-04T13:56:52.138Z\",\"updatedAt\":\"2026-08-04T13:56:53.581Z\",\"archivedAt\":null,\"creator\":{\"id\":\"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a\",\"name\":\"Aravind\"},\"updatedBy\":{\"id\":\"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a\",\"name\":\"Aravind\"},\"project\":null,\"initiative\":null,\"team\":null,\"issue\":{\"id\":\"SKI-3\",\"title\":\"Support native skill composition, dependency resolution, and verification modules\"}}"}]}

/tmp/skillplane-pr-quality-17-20-21-2026.content: {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"id\":\"ff751d37-e9fd-4c65-af99-03c92b0ef431\",\"title\":\"Ideation & Product Rationale — SKI-3: Support native skill composition, dependency resolution, and verification modules\",\"content\":\"# Ideation & Product Rationale\\n\\n**Linear issue:** [SKI-3 — Support native skill composition, dependency resolution, and verification modules](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-3/support-native-skill-composition-dependency-resolution-and>)\\n\\n## Context and motivating problem\\n\\nSkillplane delivers immutable, versioned instructions to agents, but skills are currently leaf bundles. Reuse is possible only through prose: a parent tells the agent to retrieve another skill.\\n\\nThe live prototype demonstrates that this can work. The published Add to Backlog and Issue Fix skills both point to the exact published Create and Associate Linear Issue skill, and a Linear agent successfully retrieved both parent and child versions. This removed duplicated Linear routing, idempotency, recovery, and verification guidance.\\n\\nThe prototype also exposes the product gap: Skillplane cannot identify the relationship as a dependency, ensure the child was loaded, resolve nested chains, prevent cycles, show upgrade impact, compose authorization, or attach verification obligations transitively.\\n\\nA related failure mode is execution without outcome verification. An agent can be told to use DataFn, install or scaffold it, and still route actual application reads and mutations through another path.\\n\\n## Target users and stakeholders\\n\\n* Skill authors building reusable, organization-specific agent workflows.\\n* Workspace owners governing approved stacks and operational policy.\\n* Execution agents consuming a skill to perform work.\\n* Independent verifier agents checking that the skill's required outcome actually exists.\\n* Reviewers evaluating skill amendments and dependency upgrades.\\n* Security and compliance owners who need provenance, least privilege, evidence, and revocation.\\n* Platform engineers maintaining Skillplane storage, resolver, MCP, API, UI, and observability.\\n\\n## Primary use cases\\n\\n### 1. Reusable workflow operation\\n\\nIssue Fix and Add to Backlog both depend on Create and Associate Linear Issue.\\n\\nThe parents own domain-specific preparation and authorization boundaries. The child owns Linear destination resolution, duplicate prevention, state mapping, association sequencing, partial-write recovery, and the read-back receipt.\\n\\n### 2. Company stack composition\\n\\nA Use Our Company Stack skill composes:\\n\\n* Use shadcn for UI;\\n* Use Better Auth for authentication;\\n* Use DataFn for data management;\\n* company-specific integration constraints and verification.\\n\\nThe user retrieves one logical skill while Skillplane preserves the identity and provenance of every component.\\n\\n### 3. Nested dependencies\\n\\nA child skill may itself depend on lower-level policy, framework, or verification skills. Skillplane resolves the full directed acyclic graph rather than requiring the root author to duplicate the transitive closure.\\n\\n### 4. Verification as a reusable module\\n\\nUse DataFn ships execution guidance plus blocking verification claims. The verifier must demonstrate that every relevant read surface and mutation passes through DataFn and that no unauthorized bypass exists.\\n\\n### 5. Controlled dependency upgrades\\n\\nWhen a child publishes a compatible version, existing composites remain unchanged. Skillplane offers an upgrade candidate with a dependency-closure diff for review.\\n\\n## Desired outcomes and success measures\\n\\n* Skill authors reuse common capabilities without copying Markdown.\\n* Published composites remain reproducible and content-addressable.\\n* Agents receive deterministic execution and verification plans.\\n* Dependency cycles, conflicts, authorization failures, and visibility violations are caught before publication.\\n* Reviewers can see exactly which transitive instructions and verification claims changed.\\n* Verification fails when required behavior is scaffolded but not used.\\n* Every attestation identifies the exact skill closure, implementation revision, verifier, environment, and evidence.\\n\\nPotential measures:\\n\\n* percentage of composite retrievals with a fully resolved closure;\\n* dependency-resolution and authorization failure rates;\\n* ignored or missing blocking-verification claims;\\n* dependency-upgrade candidate acceptance/rejection rates;\\n* verification pass/fail/unknown distribution;\\n* reduction in duplicated instructions across skills;\\n* time to identify which dependency introduced a changed behavior.\\n\\n## Product principles and decisions\\n\\n### Proposal: immutable resolution, not floating composition\\n\\nAuthors may declare a semantic range, but candidate creation resolves it to exact version IDs and digests. Publication never silently re-resolves to something newer.\\n\\n### Proposal: logical composition, not physical copying\\n\\nA composite is one logical resolved skill. Child bundles stay independently addressable so provenance, review history, authorization, and upgrades remain visible.\\n\\n### Proposal: structured module boundaries\\n\\nDo not concatenate arbitrary Markdown. Dependencies are named by alias and composed using explicit modes:\\n\\n* include: add the child's module to the active plan;\\n* invoke: call the child through a defined handoff boundary.\\n\\nDependencies also declare whether they apply to execution, verification, or both.\\n\\n### Proposal: verification is a first-class contract\\n\\nA skill may provide verifier instructions, structured claims, and optional probes. Blocking child claims are inherited. A parent may strengthen them but cannot silently remove them.\\n\\n### Proposal: independent verification\\n\\nExecution and verification should be separable. The verifier should be able to operate with read-only permissions and should not rely only on the executor's self-report.\\n\\n## Alternatives considered\\n\\n### Keep dependencies in Markdown only\\n\\nUseful as a prototype but not enforceable, queryable, diffable, or safely composable.\\n\\n### Copy child instructions into every parent\\n\\nSimple retrieval, but creates drift, obscures provenance, multiplies amendment work, and makes dependency upgrades hard to review.\\n\\n### Resolve current child versions at every retrieval\\n\\nConvenient but breaks immutability and reproducibility. The same parent version could behave differently tomorrow.\\n\\n### Build a single flattened bundle at authoring time\\n\\nImproves portability but loses live dependency identity unless a lock and provenance graph are retained. It also encourages file collisions and opaque override behavior.\\n\\n### Verify only package presence or imports\\n\\nInsufficient. It rewards scaffolding instead of demonstrated use across real application surfaces.\\n\\n## Product and UX considerations\\n\\n* The skill editor should provide dependency search, version constraints, aliases, scope, and mode.\\n* Candidate review should display direct and transitive dependency diffs.\\n* Skill pages should show a dependency graph, closure digest, upgrade availability, deprecation, and verification coverage.\\n* Conflict and cycle errors should name the exact path through the graph.\\n* Verification results should distinguish passed, failed, and unknown claims.\\n* The UI must make waivers explicit and auditable.\\n* Retrieval should remain simple for legacy agents while exposing a structured plan for capable clients.\\n\\n## Goals\\n\\n* Native composition, nested resolution, deterministic locks, dependency-aware review, reusable verification, and evidence-backed attestations.\\n* Backward compatibility with format-v1 leaf skills.\\n* Least-privilege authorization across the full closure.\\n* Clear operational recovery and diagnostics.\\n\\n## Non-goals\\n\\n* Automatically implementing a composed stack.\\n* Granting authorization beyond the root workflow.\\n* Auto-updating published composites.\\n* Solving arbitrary natural-language instruction conflicts.\\n* Treating verification as a single test command or package-presence check.\\n\\n## Assumptions\\n\\n* **Assumption:** Initial support can prioritize same-workspace dependencies and public cross-workspace dependencies.\\n* **Assumption:** Include and invoke cover the first practical composition cases.\\n* **Assumption:** Structured JSON claims are preferable to parsing verification requirements from Markdown.\\n* **Assumption:** Existing immutable R2 bundles and version review remain the source of truth.\\n\\n## Open questions\\n\\n* Should archive preserve pinned retrieval while a distinct revocation state blocks it?\\n* Should a dependency lock be stored in the canonical bundle, normalized database rows, or both?\\n* Can a parent explicitly waive a child claim, and which review policy must authorize that?\\n* Which evidence types need native schemas versus opaque hashed references?\\n* What resolver depth, fan-out, closure-size, and expanded-byte defaults provide a safe balance?\\n* How should incompatible instructions be declared and resolved without creating a general-purpose policy language?\\n\\n## Acceptance criteria\\n\\nAcceptance is defined on [SKI-3](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-3/support-native-skill-composition-dependency-resolution-and>). Product validation should additionally demonstrate the two motivating examples: shared Linear invocation and a company-stack composite with blocking DataFn coverage verification.\",\"icon\":null,\"color\":null,\"url\":\"https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-3-support-native-skill-composition-d5eefcd2c7b6\",\"slugId\":\"d5eefcd2c7b6\",\"createdAt\":\"2026-08-04T13:56:54.915Z\",\"updatedAt\":\"2026-08-04T13:56:56.934Z\",\"archivedAt\":null,\"creator\":{\"id\":\"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a\",\"name\":\"Aravind\"},\"updatedBy\":{\"id\":\"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a\",\"name\":\"Aravind\"},\"project\":null,\"initiative\":null,\"team\":null,\"issue\":{\"id\":\"SKI-3\",\"title\":\"Support native skill composition, dependency resolution, and verification modules\"}}"}]}

/tmp/skillplane-pr-quality-17-20-21-2026.content: {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"id\":\"0ea8e32e-7bfa-4571-add8-5229730c51e2\",\"title\":\"Architecture & Delivery Plan — SKI-15: Support local-first workspaces and resilient agent skill projections\",\"content\":\"**Backlog issue:** [SKI-15 — Support local-first workspaces and resilient agent skill projections](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-15/support-local-first-workspaces-and-resilient-agent-skill-projections>)\\n\\n## Status of this document\\n\\nThis document captures proposals and constraints from the ideation thread. It is not an approved implementation architecture. Items labeled `Proposal`, `Assumption`, and `Open question` require validation before delivery.\\n\\n## Current-state constraints\\n\\n* Skillplane's authoritative managed experience is cloud and MCP-oriented.\\n* Skills are versioned bundles containing instructions and optional supporting files.\\n* Skill creation and amendments are currently available through MCP domain tools.\\n* Agent hosts use different skill directories, metadata extensions, invocation behavior, and tool capabilities.\\n* Copying skill content to an agent directory creates a derived projection, not a new authority.\\n* Once a self-contained projection is used without contacting Skillplane, that invocation is not directly observable.\\n* Dynamic runtime content cannot safely change frontmatter or permissions that a host parsed before invocation.\\n\\n## Proposed system boundaries\\n\\n### Workspace provider\\n\\nExpose common domain operations for local and cloud authorities:\\n\\n* list and retrieve skills and immutable versions;\\n* create drafts and publish versions;\\n* propose, review, accept, and reject amendments;\\n* manage authorized contexts where supported;\\n* resolve version policies and trust requirements;\\n* emit usage events.\\n\\nProposed providers:\\n\\n* `LocalWorkspaceProvider`: embedded local metadata and content storage;\\n* `CloudWorkspaceProvider`: Skillplane Cloud API/MCP-backed authority.\\n\\n### Workspace router\\n\\nResolve qualified workspace references and account profiles. A project context contains:\\n\\n* one primary write workspace;\\n* zero or more ordered mounted sources;\\n* projection targets and policy;\\n* explicit collision resolution.\\n\\nCredentials never live in project configuration. Cloud profile secrets are stored in the OS credential store and keyed by account and endpoint.\\n\\n### Agent projection adapters\\n\\nEach adapter owns:\\n\\n* target directory discovery;\\n* supported frontmatter and command metadata;\\n* native invocation capability declarations;\\n* safe file-name and command-name mapping;\\n* projection rendering;\\n* optional deterministic live-resolution syntax;\\n* projection ownership markers and atomic updates.\\n\\nExamples include Claude-specific locations and capabilities plus generic filesystem targets. `~/.agent/skills` must not be treated as universal without an identified host contract.\\n\\n### CLI and desktop\\n\\nThe global Skillplane CLI owns setup, workspace routing, projection sync, live skill resolution, local analytics queuing, and health diagnostics. The desktop app should invoke the same operations and data model rather than implement a second setup engine.\\n\\n### MCP gateway\\n\\nMCP remains the cloud-native and ephemeral-agent transport. It exposes authorized discovery, retrieval, creation, amendments, contexts, and usage observation without requiring local projection.\\n\\n## Proposed local data model\\n\\n### Assumption: embedded metadata store\\n\\nUse an embedded transactional database such as SQLite for workspace metadata, versions, projection state, queued analytics, and mutation journals.\\n\\n### Assumption: filesystem content store\\n\\nStore immutable bundle content by digest in a filesystem content-addressed store. Metadata references exact digests and versions. Materialization never treats repository or bundle paths as trusted.\\n\\nIndicative entities:\\n\\n* `account_profile`: alias, endpoint, credential reference, principal metadata;\\n* `workspace`: stable local or cloud-qualified identity and provider;\\n* `project_context`: primary workspace, mounts, target policies;\\n* `skill` and `skill_version`: immutable identity, semantic version, digest, manifest;\\n* `projection`: target adapter, projected name, source version, policy, trust envelope;\\n* `projection_file`: path, digest, ownership marker;\\n* `usage_event`: event type, skill version, delivery mode, agent identity, timestamp, upload state;\\n* `mutation_journal`: atomic projection or import operation and recovery state.\\n\\n## Skill resolution and projection flow\\n\\n### Projection generation\\n\\n1. Resolve the project context and mounted sources.\\n2. Build the visible skill catalog and detect command-name collisions.\\n3. Resolve the selected version according to `resilient`, `strict-live`, or `pinned` policy.\\n4. Validate the bundle manifest, digest, paths, sizes, symlinks, and permitted file types.\\n5. Render host-specific frontmatter and the Skillplane freshness preamble.\\n6. Include or reference a complete fallback snapshot with source workspace, exact version, digest, and last-sync time.\\n7. Write a temporary projection tree, fsync where appropriate, and atomically replace the owned target.\\n8. Persist projection state only after the filesystem swap succeeds.\\n\\n### Invocation source precedence\\n\\nA projection defines exactly one authoritative source for each invocation:\\n\\n1. live CLI resolution when the target supports and can execute it;\\n2. Skillplane MCP retrieval when that transport is available to the agent;\\n3. CLI-managed cached resolution when allowed;\\n4. embedded snapshot fallback when allowed.\\n\\nThe agent must not merge live instructions with the embedded fallback. Host-specific adapters may make CLI resolution deterministic; generic adapters may only provide behavioral instructions.\\n\\n### Global CLI command\\n\\nHuman-facing usage can remain concise, for example `skillplane <skill-slug>`, while machine projections use an unambiguous qualified reference or projection identity.\\n\\nThe resolver receives the embedded version and digest. Expected behaviors:\\n\\n* same digest: record observed invocation and return a short directive to use the embedded snapshot;\\n* newer trusted version: return the new authoritative body and schedule projection refresh;\\n* cloud unavailable with cache permitted: identify the cached version and queue analytics locally;\\n* update expands the trust envelope: refuse automatic adoption and request approval;\\n* CLI unavailable: the projection's embedded fallback remains usable.\\n\\nNo resolver executable is copied into each skill directory.\\n\\n## Version and trust policy\\n\\nProposed version policies:\\n\\n* `latest`: newest permitted published version;\\n* `compatible`: newest version within a declared compatibility range;\\n* `pinned`: one exact immutable version.\\n\\nProposed offline policies:\\n\\n* `use-cache`: use the last verified or embedded version and disclose unverified freshness;\\n* `fail`: stop when freshness cannot be confirmed.\\n\\nThe trust envelope includes at least executable scripts, allowed tools, network behavior, host execution context, and other permission-bearing metadata. Content-only updates may be adopted under policy; permission-expanding changes require review.\\n\\n## Creation and amendment architecture\\n\\nCreation and amendment semantics belong to shared domain services rather than MCP itself. CLI, desktop, cloud API, and MCP adapt to the same operations.\\n\\nAmendments target an exact immutable base version and contain digest-checked add, replace, or delete operations plus rationale and evidence. Local workspaces may use local review policy. Cloud workspaces apply workspace authorization and approval policy. Concurrent base changes require explicit rebase or a new proposal.\\n\\nA project context's single primary write workspace determines where new skills and amendments go. Mounted sources remain read sources unless the user explicitly chooses a different write destination.\\n\\n## Analytics and observability\\n\\nDefine separate events rather than one ambiguous usage counter:\\n\\n* `skill_projected`: a version was installed into an agent target;\\n* `skill_resolved`: CLI or MCP delivered or confirmed an exact version;\\n* `skill_invoked_observed`: the host path reached Skillplane for an invocation;\\n* `skill_action_called`: a Skillplane tool or bundled instrumented action ran;\\n* `skill_completion_reported`: the agent reported finishing;\\n* `skill_success_verified`: an independent verifier confirmed defined success criteria.\\n\\nEvent dimensions may include workspace, skill and version, projection, agent product, pseudonymous installation, session identifier when available, delivery mode, freshness state, and confidence. Agent-provided model identity is declared metadata unless a trusted host asserts it.\\n\\nLocal events queue transactionally in the embedded store. Upload is opt-in for personal local workspaces and policy-controlled for organizations. Dashboards must label counts as observed and disclose unobservable embedded fallback usage.\\n\\n## MCP-only ephemeral environments\\n\\nAn ephemeral agent receives the Skillplane MCP endpoint, a short-lived scoped credential, and workspace context. MCP supplies discovery, retrieval, creation, amendment, and analytics. No local database, desktop app, or projection is required.\\n\\nNative slash-command availability remains a host capability. If the ephemeral platform cannot register prompts or commands dynamically from MCP, Skillplane provides retrieval and use but does not claim native slash commands.\\n\\n## Security and privacy\\n\\n* Store account credentials only in an operating-system credential store or equivalent protected secret service.\\n* Never embed credentials in projections or project configuration.\\n* Qualify workspace and skill identity to prevent cross-account slug confusion.\\n* Validate bundle paths against traversal and symlink escape.\\n* Enforce compressed and expanded size limits, file-count limits, and permitted media types.\\n* Treat skill content and scripts as untrusted until covered by the active trust policy.\\n* Sign or digest projection manifests so divergence and local edits are detectable.\\n* Keep local analytics local by default unless consent or organization policy authorizes upload.\\n* Avoid identifying a human from an agent invocation unless the authenticated transport already establishes that identity.\\n\\n## Reliability and recovery\\n\\n* Projection writes are journaled, idempotent, and atomic per target.\\n* Existing user-owned files are never silently overwritten.\\n* Interrupted sync resumes or rolls back from the mutation journal.\\n* Cloud outages cannot corrupt local workspace authority.\\n* Authentication expiry affects cloud resolution but not permitted local fallback.\\n* A failed association between a projection and state record is detected during the next health check.\\n* `skillplane doctor` reports missing CLI integration, stale projections, divergent files, credential failures, unresolved collisions, and pending trust approvals.\\n\\n## Migration and compatibility\\n\\n1. Inventory existing user-managed and Skillplane-managed agent skill directories.\\n2. Introduce projection ownership manifests without adopting unrelated files.\\n3. Import existing Skillplane projections as pinned snapshots where provenance can be verified.\\n4. Allow users to choose resilient or strict-live policy before enabling runtime checks.\\n5. Preserve static export as a fallback for unsupported agent hosts.\\n6. Add cloud profiles without converting local workspaces automatically.\\n\\nRollback removes only files proven to be owned by the selected projection and restores the previous owned projection tree. It does not delete local workspace data or unrelated agent skills.\\n\\n## Proposed delivery sequence\\n\\n### Phase 1: contracts and capability model\\n\\nDefine workspace providers, project contexts, qualified selectors, projection adapter capabilities, version/offline policies, trust envelopes, and analytics semantics.\\n\\n### Phase 2: embedded local workspace\\n\\nImplement local immutable skill/version operations, content storage, credential-independent local setup, and explicit import/export.\\n\\n### Phase 3: global CLI and projections\\n\\nImplement account profiles, primary-plus-mount routing, atomic projection sync, ownership manifests, collision handling, and diagnostics.\\n\\n### Phase 4: resilient runtime resolution\\n\\nAdd freshness checks, exact digest confirmation, cached fallback, trust-policy gating, and target-specific deterministic integrations where supported.\\n\\n### Phase 5: shared creation and amendments\\n\\nExpose the common domain operations through local CLI/desktop and cloud MCP, retaining immutable exact-base semantics.\\n\\n### Phase 6: analytics and privacy controls\\n\\nAdd local event queues, cloud ingestion, delivery-mode/confidence reporting, opt-in controls, and dashboards that disclose coverage.\\n\\n### Phase 7: desktop and nontechnical onboarding\\n\\nBuild the desktop wizard and initialization-skill flow on the same setup engine; add one-command bootstrap packaging and recovery UX.\\n\\n## Validation strategy\\n\\n* Contract tests run against both local and cloud workspace providers.\\n* Projection golden tests cover every supported target's paths, metadata, and content.\\n* Fault injection covers interruption before write, during swap, and before state commit.\\n* Security tests cover traversal, symlink escape, digest mismatch, decompression limits, executable scripts, and permission expansion.\\n* Multi-account tests cover identical slugs, expired credentials, profile switching, and explicit write destinations.\\n* Offline tests cover cached and strict failure policies.\\n* Analytics tests verify event boundaries, local queue replay, idempotency, and disclosed coverage.\\n* Ephemeral MCP tests prove operation without local files and reject unauthorized cross-workspace access.\\n* User-flow tests cover one-command installation, desktop setup, uninstall ownership, and recovery.\\n\\n## Risks and tradeoffs\\n\\n* Inline embedded content maximizes compatibility but always consumes context and can coexist with newer live output.\\n* Sibling fallback content reduces normal context but depends on the host's ability to read supporting files.\\n* Behavioral freshness instructions can be skipped by an agent; deterministic injection is host-specific.\\n* Following latest content reduces reproducibility; pinned mode reduces amendment immediacy.\\n* Rich analytics can conflict with local privacy expectations if defaults are not conservative.\\n* Supporting many agent adapters may create a long-lived compatibility burden.\\n* A broad first release risks coupling local storage, sync, desktop, analytics, and MCP changes; phased contracts are essential.\\n\\n## Open questions\\n\\n* Confirm the embedded storage technology and backup/export format.\\n* Choose the default fallback layout: inline body or sibling snapshot.\\n* Define the first supported agent-adapter matrix and exact guarantees.\\n* Decide whether live resolution updates the projection synchronously, asynchronously, or only on explicit sync.\\n* Define organization-level controls over offline fallback and analytics upload.\\n* Select collision UX and stable alias rules.\\n* Determine whether local-to-cloud replication remains permanently explicit or becomes a later opt-in capability.\",\"icon\":null,\"color\":null,\"url\":\"https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-15-support-local-first-workspaces-9f8209e784e5\",\"slugId\":\"9f8209e784e5\",\"createdAt\":\"2026-08-30T12:31:34.049Z\",\"updatedAt\":\"2026-08-30T12:31:34.663Z\",\"archivedAt\":null,\"creator\":{\"id\":\"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a\",\"name\":\"Aravind\"},\"updatedBy\":{\"id\":\"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a\",\"name\":\"Aravind\"},\"project\":null,\"initiative\":null,\"team\":null,\"issue\":{\"id\":\"SKI-15\",\"title\":\"Support local-first workspaces and resilient agent skill projections\"}}"}]}

/tmp/skillplane-pr-quality-17-20-21-2026.content: {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"id\":\"568038ca-a020-45ef-a3f2-d77f8cd2f681\",\"title\":\"Ideation & Product Rationale — SKI-15: Support local-first workspaces and resilient agent skill projections\",\"content\":\"**Backlog issue:** [SKI-15 — Support local-first workspaces and resilient agent skill projections](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-15/support-local-first-workspaces-and-resilient-agent-skill-projections>)\\n\\n## Context and motivating problem\\n\\nSkillplane needs an onboarding and runtime model that is useful beyond the managed cloud. The discussion started from a desired one-command initialization experience that can eventually install the CLI and desktop app, while also serving nontechnical users through an agent-driven initialization skill.\\n\\nThe scope then expanded to the operating model required underneath that onboarding:\\n\\n* use Skillplane locally without Skillplane managed cloud;\\n* expose Skillplane skills through agent-recognized filesystem directories and native slash commands;\\n* combine local and cloud workspaces, including multiple cloud accounts;\\n* understand how often skills are used and which agent used them;\\n* preserve skill creation and amendment flows currently exposed through MCP;\\n* support ephemeral cloud agents that have MCP but no persistent local filesystem;\\n* retain a usable fallback when the CLI, MCP, authentication, or network is unavailable.\\n\\nThe central product tension is freshness and observability versus resilience. A static skill projection keeps working but can become stale and invisible to analytics. A thin runtime launcher can resolve the latest instructions and record invocation, but it creates a hard runtime dependency. A hybrid projection attempts to preserve both properties honestly.\\n\\n## Target users and stakeholders\\n\\n### Individual local user\\n\\nWants Skillplane on one machine without creating or depending on a managed-cloud account. Expects a straightforward installer, offline operation, and native skills inside familiar agents.\\n\\n### Nontechnical user\\n\\nWants the desktop app or an initialization skill to discover agents, configure directories, and explain account/workspace choices without requiring shell expertise.\\n\\n### Developer using several agents\\n\\nWants the same Skillplane catalog available in Claude, Codex, Cursor, or other supported hosts while retaining host-specific discovery and invocation behavior.\\n\\n### Multi-account professional\\n\\nHas personal and work cloud accounts plus local project workspaces. Needs unambiguous resolution, safe credential storage, and a clear destination for new skills and amendments.\\n\\n### Workspace administrator\\n\\nWants controlled updates, provenance, permission review, useful adoption analytics, and no silent expansion of a skill's trust envelope.\\n\\n### Ephemeral cloud agent\\n\\nHas no durable filesystem or desktop application. It must discover, retrieve, create, and amend authorized skills through MCP alone.\\n\\n## Desired user journeys\\n\\n### First-time initialization\\n\\n1. The user installs Skillplane through a one-command bootstrap or desktop installer.\\n2. Setup discovers supported agents and their recognized skill directories.\\n3. The user can start with a local workspace, sign into one or more cloud accounts, or do both.\\n4. Setup creates an explicit project context with one primary write workspace and optional mounted skill sources.\\n5. Skillplane projects selected skills and reports exactly what it created.\\n\\n### Native skill invocation\\n\\n1. The user invokes a projected skill through an agent's native command or automatic discovery.\\n2. The projection prefers Skillplane CLI resolution, or Skillplane MCP when that is the available transport.\\n3. Live resolution checks the bundled version and digest, records an observed invocation, and returns newer permitted instructions only when needed.\\n4. If neither transport is available, the agent uses the embedded snapshot and discloses its version and unverified freshness.\\n5. The agent uses exactly one instruction source rather than merging live and fallback instructions.\\n\\n### Multiple accounts and workspaces\\n\\n1. The user signs into named profiles such as work and personal; credentials remain in the operating-system credential store.\\n2. A project chooses one primary workspace for writes and ordered mounts for additional skills.\\n3. Skill references remain qualified internally so identical slugs do not resolve accidentally across accounts.\\n4. Creation and amendments always have an explicit write destination.\\n\\n### Ephemeral MCP-only agent\\n\\n1. The environment receives a Skillplane MCP endpoint and short-lived scoped credentials.\\n2. The agent discovers and retrieves skills without installing filesystem projections.\\n3. Retrieval and mutation events are observed by the service.\\n4. Native slash commands are available only if the host separately supports dynamic MCP prompts or commands; Skillplane does not claim this universally.\\n\\n## Ideas discussed\\n\\n### Proposal: one canonical setup engine\\n\\nThe CLI command, desktop wizard, bootstrap script, and initialization skill should call the same idempotent setup operations. The public installation surface can be simple while avoiding duplicated configuration logic.\\n\\n### Proposal: local and cloud as workspace providers\\n\\nLocal storage and Skillplane Cloud should expose the same domain capabilities through different providers. CLI, desktop, API, and MCP are transports into those capabilities rather than separate implementations.\\n\\n### Proposal: primary workspace plus mounts\\n\\nA project should have exactly one primary write workspace and zero or more mounted sources. This supports simultaneous local and multi-account cloud access without making the destination of skill creation or amendments ambiguous.\\n\\n### Preferred direction under discussion: resilient projections\\n\\nProjected skills remain self-contained and contain a versioned fallback snapshot. Their first instruction asks the agent to retrieve or verify the skill through the global Skillplane CLI or MCP when available, then use the embedded content only as fallback. No resolver executable is copied into each skill folder.\\n\\n### Proposal: policy modes\\n\\n* `resilient`: prefer live resolution and fall back to the packaged snapshot;\\n* `strict-live`: require a successful freshness check and observed invocation;\\n* `pinned`: use an exact immutable packaged version.\\n\\n### Proposal: honest analytics\\n\\nSkillplane should distinguish projection/install, live retrieval or invocation, downstream Skillplane tool activity, reported completion, and independently verified success. Embedded use without CLI or MCP contact is unobservable and must not be presented as complete usage.\\n\\n## Alternatives and tradeoffs\\n\\n### Static projection only\\n\\nPros: portable, inspectable, offline, low runtime complexity. Cons: stale content, delayed amendments, no direct invocation analytics, and repeated sync work.\\n\\n### Thin runtime launcher only\\n\\nPros: latest policy enforcement, single authoritative body, smaller projection, stronger observed analytics. Cons: CLI/MCP/auth/network failures can make the native skill unusable, which is unfriendly for local and nontechnical users.\\n\\n### Agent hooks\\n\\nPros: can observe lifecycle events in supported hosts. Cons: host-specific, operationally invasive, and unavailable in many ephemeral or generic agent environments. The discussion favored projection-driven resolution as the primary mechanism rather than making hooks mandatory.\\n\\n### Resolver executable in every skill directory\\n\\nPros: can normalize command-missing and fallback behavior. Cons: duplicates runtime logic, complicates trust and updates, and turns each projection into a mini application. The discussion explicitly simplified this to one global CLI plus self-contained projected skills.\\n\\n### Automatic bidirectional local/cloud synchronization\\n\\nPros: seamless movement across devices and authorities. Cons: introduces conflict resolution, offline mutation reconciliation, authorization semantics, and difficult failure modes. The current proposal keeps authorities separate and uses explicit publish/import operations initially.\\n\\n## Desired outcomes and success measures\\n\\n* A local-only user can initialize and use Skillplane without a cloud account.\\n* A nontechnical user can complete setup without manually editing agent configuration files.\\n* Supported agents discover projected skills in their native locations.\\n* The common case confirms the embedded version without duplicating the whole skill body in context.\\n* Accepted amendments become available through the declared freshness policy.\\n* No projection update overwrites unrelated user content.\\n* Analytics dashboards label observed scope and delivery mode instead of implying complete totals.\\n* Ephemeral MCP-only agents have the same authorized domain operations even though they lack filesystem projection.\\n* Permission-expanding updates require explicit approval.\\n\\n## Product, UX, and operational considerations\\n\\n* Setup must explain local-only, connected, and MCP-only modes in user language.\\n* Account and workspace selectors should use friendly aliases while preserving qualified internal identity.\\n* A stale fallback should display its exact version and last synchronization time.\\n* Errors should distinguish CLI unavailable, authentication expired, cloud unreachable, policy-blocked update, and corrupt projection.\\n* Projection conflicts should be surfaced before writes and resolved through aliases, namespaces, or explicit precedence.\\n* The desktop app can later visualize sources, projection health, pending trust approvals, and locally queued analytics.\\n\\n## Goals\\n\\n* Deliver a coherent local-first and connected Skillplane experience.\\n* Make native agent skill discovery resilient.\\n* Preserve current cloud MCP capabilities.\\n* Establish truthful freshness, trust, and analytics semantics.\\n\\n## Non-goals\\n\\n* Guarantee universal slash-command behavior across all agents.\\n* Guarantee observation of completely disconnected fallback usage.\\n* Implement automatic local/cloud replication in the first iteration.\\n* Approve implementation, staffing, dates, or deployment through this backlog item.\\n\\n## Assumptions\\n\\n* **Assumption:** The CLI will be installed for the normal local experience even though projections must retain a fallback.\\n* **Assumption:** Agent-specific projection adapters are required because no universal skill directory or execution behavior exists.\\n* **Assumption:** Local analytics should remain local unless the user or organization explicitly enables upload.\\n\\n## Open questions\\n\\n* Is SQLite plus filesystem content storage the correct first embedded local provider?\\n* Should the fallback body live
