      workspaceId: source.workspace_id,
      skillId: source.skill_id,
      workspace: source.workspace_slug,
      skill: source.skill_slug,
      semanticVersion: source.semantic_version,
      digest: source.content_digest,
      closureDigest: await compositionDigest(source.content_digest, lock),
      expandedBytes: source.bundle.manifest.expandedByteSize,
    };
  }
  private async choices(
    dependency: SkillDependency,
    principal: Principal,
  ): Promise<DependencyChoice[]> {
    const workspace = await this.controlPool.query<{ id: string }>(
      "SELECT id FROM workspaces WHERE slug = $1",
      [dependency.workspace],
    );
    const workspaceId = workspace.rows[0]?.id;
    if (!workspaceId) this.denied();
    const rows = await this.pool.query<{
      id: string;
      semantic_version: string;
      manifest: { expandedByteSize: number };
    }>(
      `SELECT v.id,v.semantic_version,v.manifest FROM skill_versions v JOIN skills s ON s.id = v.skill_id
      LEFT JOIN skill_version_lifecycle lifecycle ON lifecycle.version_id = v.id
      WHERE s.workspace_id = $1 AND s.slug = $2 AND v.status = 'published'
      WHERE s.workspace_id = $1 AND s.slug = $2 AND v.status = 'published'
      AND (s.workspace_id = $3 OR (s.visibility = 'public' AND s.archived_at IS NULL)) AND lifecycle.revoked_at IS NULL AND ($4::text IS NULL OR v.semantic_version=$4)
      ORDER BY v.revision DESC LIMIT 101`,
      [workspaceId, dependency.skill, principal.workspaceId, valid(dependency.version)],
    );
    let ids = rows.rows
      .filter((r) => satisfies(r.semantic_version, dependency.version))
      .map((r) => r.id);
    if (!ids.length && workspaceId !== principal.workspaceId) {
      const publicRows = await this.controlPool.query<{
        version_id: string;
        semantic_version: string;
      }>(
        `SELECT p.version_id,p.semantic_version FROM public_skill_projections p JOIN public_skill_projection_heads h
        ON h.workspace_id = p.workspace_id AND h.skill_id = p.skill_id AND h.state = 'published'
        WHERE p.workspace_slug = $1 AND p.skill_slug = $2 AND p.state = 'published' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public_skill_version_lifecycle l WHERE l.version_id=p.version_id AND (l.revoked_at IS NOT NULL OR h.projection_sequence<=l.withdrawn_sequence)) AND ($3::text IS NULL OR p.semantic_version=$3) ORDER BY p.published_at DESC LIMIT 101`,
        [dependency.workspace, dependency.skill, valid(dependency.version)],
      );
      ids = publicRows.rows
        .filter((r) => satisfies(r.semantic_version, dependency.version))
        .map((r) => r.version_id);
    }
    if (ids.length > 100)
      throw new DomainError(
        "SKILL_DEPENDENCY_CONFLICT",
        "Too many dependency versions; use a narrower publication catalog",
        409,
      );
    const choices: DependencyChoice[] = [];
    let expandedBytes = 0;
    for (const id of ids) {
      const source = await this.source(id, principal);
      expandedBytes += source.bundle.manifest.expandedByteSize;
      if (expandedBytes > COMPOSITION_LIMITS.expandedBytes)
        throw new DomainError(
          "SKILL_DEPENDENCY_CONFLICT",
          "Dependency version search exceeds expanded byte budget; use a narrower range",
          409,
        );
      choices.push({ node: await this.node(source), lock: this.lock(source.bundle) });
    }
    return choices;
  }
  // Only the authored root is needed to replace unsafe pins. Never return child content.
  async upgradeBundle(versionId: string, skillId: string, principal: Principal) {
    authorize(principal, "skills:write");
    const source = await this.source(versionId, principal);
    if (
      source.workspace_id !== principal.workspaceId ||
      source.skill_id !== skillId ||
      source.status !== "published"
    )
      this.denied();
    return source.bundle;
  }
  async upgradePreview(versionId: string, principal: Principal, skillId?: string) {
    authorize(principal, "skills:read");
    const source = await this.source(versionId, principal);
    if (
      (skillId && source.skill_id !== skillId) ||
      source.workspace_id !== principal.workspaceId ||
      source.status !== "published"
    )
      this.denied();
    const before = this.lock(source.bundle);
    const prepared = await this.prepare(source.bundle, principal, source.visibility);
    const after = prepared.lock;
    return {
      available: prepared.bundle.digest !== source.bundle.digest,
      beforeClosureDigest: await compositionDigest(source.bundle.digest, before),
      afterClosureDigest: prepared.closureDigest,
      added: after.nodes.filter(
        (n) => !before.nodes.some((b) => b.versionId === n.versionId),
      ),
      removed: before.nodes.filter(
        (n) => !after.nodes.some((a) => a.versionId === n.versionId),
      ),
      beforeEdges: before.edges,
      afterEdges: after.edges,
    };
  }
  async prepare(
    bundle: CanonicalBundle,
    principal: Principal,
    visibility: string,
    preserveLock = false,
  ): Promise<PreparedComposition> {
    const started = performance.now();
    try {
      const result = await this.prepareBundle(
        bundle,
        principal,
        visibility,
        preserveLock,
      );
      if (bundle.skill.formatVersion === 2)
        console.info(
          JSON.stringify({
            event: "skill.resolution.completed",
            nodes: result.lock.nodes.length,
            elapsedMs: Math.round(performance.now() - started),
          }),
        );
      return result;
    } catch (error) {
      console.info(
        JSON.stringify({
          event: "skill.resolution.failed",
          code: error instanceof DomainError ? error.code : "INTERNAL_ERROR",
          elapsedMs: Math.round(performance.now() - started),
        }),
      );
      throw error;
    }
  }
  private async prepareBundle(
    bundle: CanonicalBundle,
    principal: Principal,
    visibility: string,
    preserveLock = false,
  ): Promise<PreparedComposition> {
    if (bundle.skill.formatVersion === 1)
      return {
        bundle,
        lock: emptyLock(),
        closureDigest: await compositionDigest(bundle.digest, emptyLock()),
      };
    if (!this.writesEnabled)
      throw new DomainError(
        "SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE",
        "Composition writes are disabled",
        503,
      );
    authorize(principal, "skills:read");
    const files = new Map(bundle.files);
    files.delete("skill.lock.json");
    const authored = await canonicalizeBundleFiles({ skill: bundle.skill, files });
    const root = {
      workspace: await this.workspaceSlug(principal.workspaceId),
      skill: bundle.skill.slug,
      expandedBytes: authored.manifest.expandedByteSize,
    };
    const lock = preserveLock
      ? this.lock(bundle)
      : await resolveDependencies({
          dependencies: bundle.skill.dependencies,
          root,
          choices: (d) => this.choices(d, principal),
        });
    validateLock(lock, root);
    await this.revalidate(lock, principal, visibility);
    files.set("skill.lock.json", new TextEncoder().encode(`${stableJson(lock)}\n`));
    const canonical = await canonicalizeBundleFiles({ skill: bundle.skill, files });
    validateLock(lock, { ...root, expandedBytes: canonical.manifest.expandedByteSize });
    return {
      bundle: canonical,
      lock,
      closureDigest: await compositionDigest(canonical.digest, lock),
    };
  }
  async revalidate(
    lock: DependencyLock,
    principal: Principal | null,
    visibility: string,
    db: Queryable = this.pool,
  ): Promise<Map<string, Source>> {
    const sources = new Map<string, Source>();
    for (const locked of lock.nodes) {
      const source = await this.source(locked.versionId, principal, db);
      if (source.status !== "published") this.denied();
      if (
        (visibility === "public" || source.workspace_id !== principal?.workspaceId) &&
        source.visibility !== "public"
      )
        this.denied();
      if (visibility === "workspace" && source.visibility === "private") this.denied();
      if (stableJson(await this.node(source)) !== stableJson(locked))
        throw new DomainError(
          "SKILL_DEPENDENCY_CONFLICT",
          "Locked dependency identity changed",
          409,
        );
      sources.set(locked.versionId, source);
    }
    return sources;
  }
  async persist(
    client: PoolClient,
    versionId: string,
    workspaceId: string,
    prepared: PreparedComposition,
  ): Promise<void> {
    if (prepared.bundle.skill.formatVersion === 1) return;
    for (const edge of prepared.lock.edges) {
      const child = prepared.lock.nodes.find((n) => n.versionId === edge.child);
      if (!child) this.denied();
      await client.query(
        `INSERT INTO skill_version_dependencies (workspace_id, root_version_id, parent_version_id, alias, ordinal, child_version_id, edge, node)
        VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6,$7,$8)`,
        [
          workspaceId,
          versionId,
          edge.parent === "$root" ? versionId : edge.parent,
          edge.alias,
          edge.ordinal,
          edge.child,
          edge,
          child,
        ],
      );
    }
    await client.query(
      `INSERT INTO skill_version_compositions (workspace_id,version_id,format_version,dependency_closure_digest,dependency_lock)
      VALUES ($1,$2,2,$3,$4)`,
      [workspaceId, versionId, prepared.closureDigest, prepared.lock],
    );
  }
  async validatePublication(
    versionId: string,
    principal: Principal,
    visibility: string,
    db: Queryable,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const result = await db.query<{
      format_version: number;
      dependency_lock: DependencyLock | null;
      dependency_closure_digest: string | null;
    }>(
      "SELECT (v.manifest->>'formatVersion')::integer AS format_version,c.dependency_lock,c.dependency_closure_digest FROM skill_versions v LEFT JOIN skill_version_compositions c ON c.version_id=v.id AND c.workspace_id=v.workspace_id WHERE v.id=$1 AND v.workspace_id=$2",
      [versionId, principal.workspaceId],
    );
    const row = result.rows[0];
    if (row?.format_version === 2) {
      if (!this.writesEnabled)
        throw new DomainError(
          "SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE",
          "Composition writes are disabled",
          503,
        );
      if (!row.dependency_lock || !row.dependency_closure_digest)
        throw new DomainError(
          "SKILL_DEPENDENCY_CONFLICT",
          "Candidate has no immutable normalized lock",
          409,
        );
      const source = await this.source(versionId, principal, db);
      if (
        stableJson(row.dependency_lock) !== stableJson(this.lock(source.bundle)) ||
        row.dependency_closure_digest !== (await this.node(source)).closureDigest
      )
        throw new DomainError(
          "SKILL_DEPENDENCY_CONFLICT",
          "Candidate lock disagrees with its canonical bundle",
          409,
        );
      await this.revalidate(row.dependency_lock, principal, visibility, db);
    }
  }

  async resolve(
    versionId: string,
    principal: Principal | null,
    purpose: "execute" | "verify" = "execute",
    allowCandidate = false,
  ): Promise<CompositionPlan> {
    if (principal) authorize(principal, "skills:read");
    const source = await this.source(versionId, principal);
    if (
      source.status !== "published" &&
      !(
        allowCandidate &&
        principal &&
        principal.role !== "viewer" &&
        source.workspace_id === principal.workspaceId &&
        (principal.kind === "user" || principal.scopes.includes("skills:amend"))
      )
    )
      this.denied();
    const root = await this.node(source);
    const lock = this.lock(source.bundle);
    const sources = await this.revalidate(lock, principal, source.visibility);
    sources.set(versionId, source);
    const executionIds = new Set<string>();
    const verificationIds = new Set<string>();
    const visit = (id: string, execution: boolean) => {
      const parent = id === versionId ? "$root" : id;
      if (execution && executionIds.has(id)) return;
      if (!execution && verificationIds.has(id)) return;
      for (const edge of lock.edges.filter((e) => e.parent === parent))
        visit(edge.child, execution && edge.scope !== "verification");
      verificationIds.add(id);
      if (execution) executionIds.add(id);
    };
    visit(versionId, true);
    const module = (id: string, verify: boolean): ResolvedModule | null => {
      const s = sources.get(id);
      if (!s) this.denied();
      const skill = s.bundle.skill;
      const path = verify
        ? skill.formatVersion === 2
          ? skill.entrypoints.verify
          : undefined
        : "SKILL.md";
      if (!path) return null;
      return {
        versionId: id,
        workspace: s.workspace_slug,
        skill: s.skill_slug,
        digest: s.content_digest,
        instructions: new TextDecoder().decode(s.bundle.files.get(path)),
        files: s.bundle.manifest.files,
      };
    };
    const claims: CompositionPlan["verificationPlan"]["claims"] = [];
    for (const id of verificationIds) {
      const s = sources.get(id);
      if (!s) this.denied();
      if (s.bundle.skill.formatVersion === 2 && s.bundle.skill.verification) {
        const parsed = verificationClaimsSchema.parse(
          JSON.parse(
            new TextDecoder().decode(
              s.bundle.files.get(s.bundle.skill.verification.claims),
            ),
          ),
        );
        for (const claim of parsed)
          claims.push({
            ...claim,
            namespacedId: `${id}/${claim.id}`,
            originatingVersionId: id,
          });
      }
    }
    claims.sort((a, b) =>
      a.namespacedId < b.namespacedId ? -1 : a.namespacedId > b.namespacedId ? 1 : 0,
    );
    return {
      root,
      closureDigest: root.closureDigest,
      dag: lock,
      executionPlan: {
        modules:
          purpose === "verify"
            ? []
            : [...executionIds]
                .map((id) => module(id, false))
                .filter((m): m is ResolvedModule => m !== null),
        invocations:
          purpose === "verify"
            ? []
            : lock.edges.filter(
                (e) =>
                  e.mode === "invoke" &&
                  e.scope !== "verification" &&
                  executionIds.has(e.parent === "$root" ? versionId : e.parent),
              ),
      },
      verificationPlan: {
        modules: [...verificationIds]
          .map((id) => module(id, true))
          .filter((m): m is ResolvedModule => m !== null),
        claims,
      },
      warnings: [...sources.values()]
        .filter((s) => s.deprecated_at)
        .map((s) => `Deprecated version: ${s.id}`),
    };
  }
}
"}

report-template
# PR quality analysis report template

Use a compact chat verdict plus a dated, separately identifiable full analysis. Notion publication is the default unless explicitly disabled. Read `notion-publication.md` before publishing; use `integrations.md` when falling back to Composio.

## Compact chat verdict

**<rating>/10 — <assessment>; <readiness>.**

Brief strengths and highest-impact actionable findings, with source links. State the exact reviewed head, focused test results, CI status and material limits. Link the verified Notion analysis and evidence (or the local artifact when publication is disabled/blocked). Name the reviewer harness/model when known; distinguish it from the implementation author.

Do not copy old counts, ratings or attribution into a new analysis without verification. No findings means no actionable defects found within the recorded scope, not proof of defect-free code.

## Analysis metadata

Include this block in every analysis, even if Notion has dedicated properties. Unavailable values are explicitly `unknown`; omit no distinction between author and reviewer.

```yaml
analysis_id: <stable UUID for this fresh analysis; reused for publication retry>
analysis_type: <initial | same-head | new-head | targeted-follow-up>
analysis_status: <completed | partial | blocked>
started_at: <ISO-8601 UTC>
completed_at: <ISO-8601 UTC or unknown>
previous_analysis_id: <ID/link or none>
repository: <canonical repository URL>
pr_or_session: <PR URL or source session URL>
reviewed_head: <full SHA>
base: <full SHA>
merge_base: <full SHA>
captured_at: <ISO-8601 UTC>
source_snapshot: <requirement/document snapshot IDs or digests; limits explicit>
scope: <reviewed and unreviewed surfaces>
skill: <workspace/slug@published-version>
rubric: <version or named dimensions/weights>
reviewer:
  harness_client: <name>
  harness_version: <version or unknown>
  provider: <provider or unknown>
  model: <exact ID or unknown>
  model_version: <version or unknown>
  reasoning: <setting or unknown>
  environment: <execution environment or unknown>
  task_session: <ID/link or unknown>
  attribution_source: <runtime metadata | user-supplied | other evidence | unknown>
  attribution_confidence: <high | medium | low | unknown>
  mixed_or_delegated: <material contributors/ranges or none>
implementation_author:
  harness_model: <separate author attribution>
  source_confidence: <evidence and confidence>
  commit_range: <original/remediated range>
publication:
  destination: <Notion hub | local-only | blocked>
  analysis_url: <verified URL or pending>
  evidence_url: <verified URL or unavailable>
```

Do not guess the analyst model from the implementation badge, or the implementation model from the analyst's current runtime. An application name alone may not identify the underlying harness/version. Preserve requested-vs-confirmed model distinctions.

## Issue overview

One issue overview, linked to implementation parents. Put the current comparison first:

| Implementation | Latest analysis / reviewer | Reviewed SHA | Quality | Readiness | Strength | Main gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

For a single PR, keep one row; do not invent comparators. Include source issue and acceptance/design links, recommendation, acceptance coverage, major differences and links to full analyses. Display same-head disagreement when it affects the recommendation. Use native Notion tables per the fetched Markdown specification.

## Implementation parent and analysis history

One parent per repository/PR or non-PR session. Keep an analysis index:

| Analysis ID / date | Reviewed head | Reviewer harness/model | Scope/status | Quality/verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Each fresh assessment, including the same head, has its own analysis child page or existing database row. Retain earlier snapshots and metadata. Retrying publication uses the same ID and repairs its entry; a fresh assessment receives a new ID. Do not silently replace history or average scores. Identify the latest completed or explicitly adjudicated analysis on the parent.

## Full analysis

1. **Decision and scope:** concrete problem, implemented outcome, quality and readiness, source requirements and coverage limits.
2. **Strengths and scoring:** weighted dimensions with rationale; average never overrides a blocker. Separate original code from author/third-party remediation.
3. **Findings:** severity, trigger, expected/actual behavior, user impact, exact immutable file/line, evidence status, root cause, narrow complete fix and needed validation. Distinguish reproduced, code-traced, unverified, already fixed and duplicate.
4. **Validation:** commands, reviewed SHA, runtime/dependency provenance, counts, failures, canceled/unrun checks and CI links. Classify changed-code, baseline, environment and unknown failures. Cover relevant public failure paths through artifact writing and publication/consumption, using mocks where live writes are not authorized.
5. **Author process:** observed requirement → transcript decision → code consequence → missed verification, only where evidence exists. Label inferences and absent transcripts; include a concise author follow-up about a material deviation without presuming motive.
6. **Analysis provenance and exposure:** reviewer metadata above, source/bot/transcript exposure, independent vs reused checks and any changes in reviewer model or scope. Do not claim blind/independent review when prior findings were available.
7. **Evidence:** reproducible probes, input snapshots and immutable links. Record incomplete evidence and publication state honestly.

## Evidence bundle

Provide minimal runnable probe source and commands, fixtures/setup, runtime and reused/installed dependencies, expected-vs-actual behavior, output/exit status and relevant CI/source links. Label fixture repository SHAs separately from the PR head. Redact secrets and unrelated private material. Include source scripts alongside outputs; outputs alone may be insufficient to reproduce the result.

Full transcripts are copied only when requested or otherwise authorized; default review publication includes pertinent excerpts/source links and explicit availability. Preserve timestamps/ranges and distinguish excerpts from complete transcripts. Place long evidence in child pages/attachments. Replace local-only links before publication and verify the uploaded content.

## Publication verification

Publish to the intended hub unless explicitly disabled; no redundant authorization prompt. Query for existing issue/PR/analysis identities. Read schemas and preserve existing structure. Update properties separately from content where required. Read back analysis ID, reviewer metadata, findings including the final finding, score/verdict, reviewed SHA, evidence content/links, issue relations and history. State partial writes and blockers accurately; retry with the same analysis ID.

Keep author/model aggregates in their separate scorecard. Multiple analyses of one PR do not create additional independent author samples. Preserve analysis-level disagreements rather than manufacturing a consensus or leaderboard.

notion-publication
# Default Notion publication and multiple analyses

Publish the finished review to the intended Notion QA hub unless the user explicitly opts out. The workflow grants this reporting default; do not add a confirmation gate merely because Notion is external. Respect an explicit local-only/chat-only/no-external-writes instruction. Confirm the intended workspace/destination from current connection and existing context; ambiguity requires destination clarification, not a new permission question. Do not broaden sharing, create a public site or modify unrelated pages.

## Reuse identity, preserve analysis history

- One issue overview per canonical repository/issue context; one implementation parent per repository/PR (or non-PR session).
- One analysis record/child page per fresh assessment, even at the same head and by the same reviewer. Generate `analysis_id` once (UUID is suitable), keep it in the report and evidence, and preserve it across upload retries/corrections to that analysis.
- A new assessment has a new analysis ID, timestamps, reviewer metadata, findings, score, validation and evidence. Link `previous_analysis_id` / `supersedes_analysis_id` when applicable without deleting the prior result. A changed head is not required for a new analysis.
- Prefer the hub's existing analysis-history database when present. If the schema has only one Implementation Review per PR, keep that parent and create analysis child pages with an index table. Do not create duplicate PR parents or remodel unrelated databases. For legacy parents containing a single review, preserve the existing content as historical and append/index the new analysis; do not retroactively invent unknown reviewer metadata.
- Use `(repository, PR/session, analysis_id)` for publication deduplication. A retry updates the matching record. Never deduplicate distinct analyses solely by head SHA, model or date.
- The issue overview and PR parent can display the latest completed analysis, with its analysis ID, timestamp, reviewer and reviewed SHA. A partial or blocked new analysis does not silently replace a prior completed verdict. Same-head disagreements remain visible; do not merge findings or average scores without adjudication.

## Required analysis metadata

Separate **implementation author** from **analysis performer** in both labels and data. Record:

- Analysis ID; start/completion timestamps; status; scope; reason/type (initial, same-head independent assessment, new-head re-review, targeted follow-up); prior analysis link when relevant.
- Repository/PR/session; reviewed head, base and merge base; capture/freshness time; requirement/source snapshot identities; skill slug, published version and report/rubric version.
- Reviewer harness/client and version, provider, exact model/version, reasoning setting, execution environment, task/session ID/link; source and confidence for this attribution. Record mixed turns or delegated reviewers where material. Use explicit `unknown` rather than inferring identity from the current app label or implementation author.
- Author harness/model provenance separately, with the original-vs-remediated commit range and evidence/confidence.
- Findings, score dimensions/verdict, commands/probes, dependency environment, coverage gaps and publication state.

Do not repurpose an existing Author Harness/Model column as reviewer metadata. Put analysis metadata in dedicated properties if the schema supports them and always in the analysis body. If schema changes are unnecessary, the child-page body and index are sufficient.

## Publication sequence

1. Fetch connection identity, hub, schemas and current issue/PR entries. Query all necessary pages to establish duplicates/history. Fetch the enhanced Markdown spec when required by the tool. Use direct Notion first, then Composio on access failure; reuse schemas and IDs throughout.
2. Prepare a concise issue overview, full analysis, and an evidence child page/bundle. Keep comparison first, detailed findings below, transcripts behind links. Never label missing transcripts as copied or verified.
3. Publish the analysis and evidence using the stable analysis ID. Include runnable minimal probe scripts/commands, fixtures/setup, runtime/dependencies, stdout/stderr and exit statuses, expected-vs-actual behavior, immutable code/source links, and redaction notes. Label fixture SHAs separately from reviewed PR SHAs. Use mocks for unapproved external writes and dummy secrets for credential probes.
4. Replace local filesystem links with uploaded files or Notion evidence references. Do not publish broken `/tmp/...` links. If a full log or script cannot be uploaded, preserve the minimal reproducible recipe and explicitly list the unavailable evidence; do not call an output-only dump a complete reproduction bundle.
5. Update the parent/index, issue relations and hub summary narrowly, preserving unrelated wording and historical analyses. Compute counts from actual records: issue count, unique implementation count and analysis count are different. Do not inflate author scorecard sample counts when adding another analysis of the same PR.
6. Use **separate `update_properties` and `update_content` operations** where the connector treats them separately. In the observed direct connector, `update_content` returned success while ignoring accompanying properties. Do not assume properties applied because content did. Inspect current schemas/help for Composio equivalents instead of copying direct-tool arguments.
7. Read back every material write: full finding set and tail, native tables, reviewer/author metadata, score/verdict, SHA, analysis ID, evidence URLs, both directions of relations and retained history. Verify evidence content, not just the existence of a child page. Check truncation/unknown blocks and pagination. Repair partial property/link writes without duplicating pages.
8. Final response: verified analysis URL, issue overview if useful, and concise publication limitations. If publication remains blocked after fallback, say what succeeded and what remains, and keep the same analysis ID for continuation.

## Scorecards

Keep author-implementation quality and reviewer-analysis quality separate. Multiple reviewers assessing one PR are paired analyses of one implementation, not independent author samples. Preserve per-analysis scores and disagreements; choose a latest/adjudicated summary explicitly and retain the decision trail. Update aggregate counts only when the existing rubric and denominator justify it. Publishing a review does not authorize inventing a model leaderboard.

A partial or blocked new analysis does not silently replace a prior completed verdict. Same-head disagreements remain visible; do not merge findings or average scores without adjudication.

## Required analysis metadata

Separate **implementation author** from **analysis performer** in both labels and data. Record:

- Analysis ID; start/completion timestamps; status; scope; reason/type (initial, same-head independent assessment, new-head re-review, targeted follow-up); prior analysis link when relevant.
- Repository/PR/session; reviewed head, base and merge base; capture/freshness time; requirement/source snapshot identities; skill slug, published version and report/rubric version.
- Reviewer harness/client and version, provider, exact model/version, reasoning setting, execution environment, task/session ID/link; source and confidence for this attribution. Record mixed turns or delegated reviewers where material. Use explicit `unknown` rather than inferring identity from the current app label or implementation author.
- Author harness/model provenance separately, with the original-vs-remediated commit range and evidence/confidence.
- Findings, score dimensions/verdict, commands/probes, dependency environment, coverage gaps and publication state.

Do not repurpose an existing Author Harness/Model column as reviewer metadata. Put analysis metadata in dedicated properties if the schema supports them and always in the analysis body. If schema changes are unnecessary, the child-page body and index are sufficient.

## Publication sequence

1. Fetch connection identity, hub, schemas and current issue/PR entries. Query all necessary pages to establish duplicates/history. Fetch the enhanced Markdown spec when required by the tool. Use direct Notion first, then Composio on access failure; reuse schemas and IDs throughout.
2. Prepare a concise issue overview, full analysis, and an evidence child page/bundle. Keep comparison first, detailed findings below, transcripts behind links. Never label missing transcripts as copied or verified.
3. Publish the analysis and evidence using the stable analysis ID. Include runnable minimal probe scripts/commands, fixtures/setup, runtime/dependencies, stdout/stderr and exit statuses, expected-vs-actual behavior, immutable code/source links, and redaction notes. Label fixture SHAs separately from reviewed PR SHAs. Use mocks for unapproved external writes and dummy secrets for credential probes.
4. Replace local filesystem links with uploaded files or Notion evidence references. Do not publish broken `/tmp/...` links. If a full log or script cannot be uploaded, preserve the minimal reproducible recipe and explicitly list the unavailable evidence; do not call an output-only dump a complete reproduction bundle.
5. Update the parent/index, issue relations and hub summary narrowly, preserving unrelated wording and historical analyses. Compute counts from actual records: issue count, unique implementation count and analysis count are different. Do not inflate author scorecard sample counts when adding another analysis of the same PR.
6. Use **separate `update_properties` and `update_content` operations** where the connector treats them separately. In the observed direct connector, `update_content` returned success while ignoring accompanying properties. Do not assume properties applied because content did. Inspect current schemas/help for Composio equivalents instead of copying direct-tool arguments.
7. Read back every material write: full finding set and tail, native tables, reviewer/author metadata, score/verdict, SHA, analysis ID, evidence URLs, both directions of relations and retained history. Verify evidence content, not just the existence of a child page. Check truncation/unknown blocks and pagination. Repair partial property/link writes without duplicating pages.
8. Final response: verified analysis URL, issue overview if useful, and concise publication limitations. If publication remains blocked after fallback, say what succeeded and what remains, and keep the same analysis ID for continuation.

## Scorecards

Keep author-implementation quality and reviewer-analysis quality separate. Multiple reviewers assessing one PR are paired analyses of one implementation, not independent author samples. Preserve per-analysis scores and disagreements; choose a latest/adjudicated summary explicitly and retain the decision trail. Update aggregate counts only when the existing rubric and denominator justify it. Publishing a review does not authorize inventing a model leaderboard.

**Backlog issue:** [SKI-15 — Support local-first workspaces and resilient agent skill projections](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-15/support-local-first-workspaces-and-resilient-agent-skill-projections>)

## Status of this document

This document captures proposals and constraints from the ideation thread. It is not an approved implementation architecture. Items labeled `Proposal`, `Assumption`, and `Open question` require validation before delivery.

## Current-state constraints

* Skillplane's authoritative managed experience is cloud and MCP-oriented.
* Skills are versioned bundles containing instructions and optional supporting files.
* Skill creation and amendments are currently available through MCP domain tools.
* Agent hosts use different skill directories, metadata extensions, invocation behavior, and tool capabilities.
* Copying skill content to an agent directory creates a derived projection, not a new authority.
* Once a self-contained projection is used without contacting Skillplane, that invocation is not directly observable.
* Dynamic runtime content cannot safely change frontmatter or permissions that a host parsed before invocation.

## Proposed system boundaries

### Workspace provider

Expose common domain operations for local and cloud authorities:

* list and retrieve skills and immutable versions;
* create drafts and publish versions;
* propose, review, accept, and reject amendments;
* manage authorized contexts where supported;
* resolve version policies and trust requirements;
* emit usage events.

Proposed providers:

* `LocalWorkspaceProvider`: embedded local metadata and content storage;
* `CloudWorkspaceProvider`: Skillplane Cloud API/MCP-backed authority.

### Workspace router

Resolve qualified workspace references and account profiles. A project context contains:

* `skill_resolved`: CLI or MCP delivered or confirmed an exact version;
* `skill_invoked_observed`: the host path reached Skillplane for an invocation;
* `skill_action_called`: a Skillplane tool or bundled instrumented action ran;
* `skill_completion_reported`: the agent reported finishing;
* `skill_success_verified`: an independent verifier confirmed defined success criteria.

* create drafts and publish versions;
* propose, review, accept, and reject amendments;
* manage authorized contexts where supported;
* resolve version policies and trust requirements;
* emit usage events.

Proposed providers:

* `LocalWorkspaceProvider`: embedded local metadata and content storage;
* `CloudWorkspaceProvider`: Skillplane Cloud API/MCP-backed authority.

### Workspace router

Resolve qualified workspace references and account profiles. A project context contains:

* one primary write workspace;
* zero or more ordered mounted sources;
* projection targets and policy;
* explicit collision resolution.

Credentials never live in project configuration. Cloud profile secrets are stored in the OS credential store and keyed by account and endpoint.

### Agent projection adapters

Each adapter owns:

* target directory discovery;
* supported frontmatter and command metadata;
* native invocation capability declarations;
* safe file-name and command-name mapping;
* projection rendering;
* optional deterministic live-resolution syntax;
* projection ownership markers and atomic updates.

Examples include Claude-specific locations and capabilities plus generic filesystem targets. `~/.agent/skills` must not be treated as universal without an identified host contract.

### CLI and desktop

The global Skillplane CLI owns setup, workspace routing, projection sync, live skill resolution, local analytics queuing, and health diagnostics. The desktop app should invoke the same operations and data model rather than implement a second setup engine.

### MCP gateway

MCP remains the cloud-native and ephemeral-agent transport. It exposes authorized discovery, retrieval, creation, amendments, contexts, and usage observation without requiring local projection.

## Proposed local data model

### Assumption: embedded metadata store

Use an embedded transactional database such as SQLite for workspace metadata, versions, projection state, queued analytics, and mutation journals.

### Assumption: filesystem content store

Store immutable bundle content by digest in a filesystem content-addressed store. Metadata references exact digests and versions. Materialization never treats repository or bundle paths as trusted.

Indicative entities:

* `account_profile`: alias, endpoint, credential reference, principal metadata;
* `workspace`: stable local or cloud-qualified identity and provider;
* `project_context`: primary workspace, mounts, target policies;
* `skill` and `skill_version`: immutable identity, semantic version, digest, manifest;
* `projection`: target adapter, projected name, source version, policy, trust envelope;
* `projection_file`: path, digest, ownership marker;
* `usage_event`: event type, skill version, delivery mode, agent identity, timestamp, upload state;
* `mutation_journal`: atomic projection or import operation and recovery state.

## Skill resolution and projection flow

### Projection generation

1. Resolve the project context and mounted sources.
2. Build the visible skill catalog and detect command-name collisions.
3. Resolve the selected version according to `resilient`, `strict-live`, or `pinned` policy.
4. Validate the bundle manifest, digest, paths, sizes, symlinks, and permitted file types.
5. Render host-specific frontmatter and the Skillplane freshness preamble.
6. Include or reference a complete fallback snapshot with source workspace, exact version, digest, and last-sync time.
7. Write a temporary projection tree, fsync where appropriate, and atomically replace the owned target.
8. Persist projection state only after the filesystem swap succeeds.

### Invocation source precedence

A projection defines exactly one authoritative source for each invocation:

1. live CLI resolution when the target supports and can execute it;
2. Skillplane MCP retrieval when that transport is available to the agent;
3. CLI-managed cached resolution when allowed;
4. embedded snapshot fallback when allowed.

The agent must not merge live instructions with the embedded fallback. Host-specific adapters may make CLI resolution deterministic; generic adapters may only provide behavioral instructions.

### Global CLI command

Human-facing usage can remain concise, for example `skillplane <skill-slug>`, while machine projections use an unambiguous qualified reference or projection identity.

The resolver receives the embedded version and digest. Expected behaviors:

* same digest: record observed invocation and return a short directive to use the embedded snapshot;
* newer trusted version: return the new authoritative body and schedule projection refresh;
* cloud unavailable with cache permitted: identify the cached version and queue analytics locally;
* update expands the trust envelope: refuse automatic adoption and request approval;
* CLI unavailable: the projection's embedded fallback remains usable.

No resolver executable is copied into each skill directory.

## Version and trust policy

Proposed version policies:

* `latest`: newest permitted published version;
* `compatible`: newest version within a declared compatibility range;
* `pinned`: one exact immutable version.

Proposed offline policies:

* `use-cache`: use the last verified or embedded version and disclose unverified freshness;
* `fail`: stop when freshness cannot be confirmed.

The trust envelope includes at least executable scripts, allowed tools, network behavior, host execution context, and other permission-bearing metadata. Content-only updates may be adopted under policy; permission-expanding changes require review.

## Creation and amendment architecture

Creation and amendment semantics belong to shared domain services rather than MCP itself. CLI, desktop, cloud API, and MCP adapt to the same operations.

Amendments target an exact immutable base version and contain digest-checked add, replace, or delete operations plus rationale and evidence. Local workspaces may use local review policy. Cloud workspaces apply workspace authorization and approval policy. Concurrent base changes require explicit rebase or a new proposal.

A project context's single primary write workspace determines where new skills and amendments go. Mounted sources remain read sources unless the user explicitly chooses a different write destination.

## Analytics and observability

Define separate events rather than one ambiguous usage counter:

* `skill_projected`: a version was installed into an agent target;
* `skill_resolved`: CLI or MCP delivered or confirmed an exact version;
* `skill_invoked_observed`: the host path reached Skillplane for an invocation;
* `skill_action_called`: a Skillplane tool or bundled instrumented action ran;
* `skill_completion_reported`: the agent reported finishing;
* `skill_success_verified`: an independent verifier confirmed defined success criteria.

Event dimensions may include workspace, skill and version, projection, agent product, pseudonymous installation, session identifier when available, delivery mode, freshness state, and confidence. Agent-provided model identity is declared metadata unless a trusted host asserts it.

Local events queue transactionally in the embedded store. Upload is opt-in for personal local workspaces and policy-controlled for organizations. Dashboards must label counts as observed and disclose unobservable embedded fallback usage.

## MCP-only ephemeral environments

An ephemeral agent receives the Skillplane MCP endpoint, a short-lived scoped credential, and workspace context. MCP supplies discovery, retrieval, creation, amendment, and analytics. No local database, desktop app, or projection is required.

Native slash-command availability remains a host capability. If the ephemeral platform cannot register prompts or commands dynamically from MCP, Skillplane provides retrieval and use but does not claim native slash commands.

## Security and privacy

* Store account credentials only in an operating-system credential store or equivalent protected secret service.
* Never embed credentials in projections or project configuration.
* Qualify workspace and skill identity to prevent cross-account slug confusion.
* Validate bundle paths against traversal and symlink escape.
* Enforce compressed and expanded size limits, file-count limits, and permitted media types.
* Treat skill content and scripts as untrusted until covered by the active trust policy.
* Sign or digest projection manifests so divergence and local edits are detectable.
* Keep local analytics local by default unless consent or organization policy authorizes upload.
* Avoid identifying a human from an agent invocation unless the authenticated transport already establishes that identity.

## Reliability and recovery

* Projection writes are journaled, idempotent, and atomic per target.
* Existing user-owned files are never silently overwritten.
* Interrupted sync resumes or rolls back from the mutation journal.
* Cloud outages cannot corrupt local workspace authority.
* Authentication expiry affects cloud resolution but not permitted local fallback.
* A failed association between a projection and state record is detected during the next health check.
* `skillplane doctor` reports missing CLI integration, stale projections, divergent files, credential failures, unresolved collisions, and pending trust approvals.

## Migration and compatibility

1. Inventory existing user-managed and Skillplane-managed agent skill directories.
2. Introduce projection ownership manifests without adopting unrelated files.

The same missing-map pattern applies to all ten new tools. Service principals still receive domain scope checks; this finding specifically concerns user OAuth tokens.','Map all ten tools to read/write/publish scopes and test under-scoped user OAuth requests through the real HTTP boundary. The probe uses the actual registered tool name and separately confirms the user-principal path.'), +('P1','Global visibility withdrawal is ignored by regional bundle reads','packages/domain/src/composition-service.ts',124,'Reproduced with actual source method and mocked storage/control rows','When a global withdrawn_sequence exists while a regional skill row is still public, source() returns the regional canonical bundle to a foreign-workspace caller. The cutoff is checked only in the public-projection branch. This defeats the documented immediate global withdrawal guarantee during propagation or regional transaction failure. No production data was accessed.','Apply the causally ordered withdrawal gate to regional public reads too, using trusted visibility sequence state; retain authorized owner access. Test a committed global withdrawal with a stale regional public row and a newer legitimate republish.'), +('P2','New catalog exceeds the existing Linear client budget','mcp/src/server.ts',218,'Reproduced over local MCP HTTP conformance','The new 37-tool catalog compacts to 41,678 bytes for the Linear OAuth client, above the existing 32,768-byte contract. Conformance fails on size and on the stale 27-tool inventory assertion. Updating the count alone leaves the compatibility regression. A live Linear connection was not exercised.','Reduce or partition the advertised client catalog while preserving required tool access, and update the complete inventory expectations. Keep the 32 KiB compatibility assertion and verify live Linear discovery.'), +('P2','A public parent can publish an archived public dependency','packages/domain/src/composition-service.ts',410,'Reproduced against fresh PostgreSQL','Creating a public child, archiving it, and creating a public parent in the same workspace succeeds. source() allows same-workspace archived pins; revalidate() checks visibility but not archive/public availability. Anonymous reads reject that archived child, so the newly published public parent cannot deliver its closure. Preserving private same-workspace archived pins is valid; publishing a publicly unusable closure is the defect.','For public parent creation/publication, validate anonymous/public availability for every node, including archive and withdrawal status. Keep private pinned archive semantics intact.'), +('P2','MCP rejects authorized unpublished composite retrieval','mcp/src/tools/retrieve.ts',97,'Code-traced','resolveVersion authorizes a pending v2 candidate and resolves it with allowCandidate=true. skillRetrieve then resolves the same version again with the default false; skillResolve repeats this mismatch. Authors therefore cannot retrieve/resolve a candidate that the first authorization step explicitly admitted.','Pass the established candidate-read authorization through both final composition calls and add end-to-end owner candidate retrieval/resolve tests, plus viewer and foreign-principal denial controls.'), +('P2','Redacted evidence validation accepts token fragments','packages/domain/src/verification.ts',273,'Reproduced validation boundary with mocked idempotency replay','addEvidence rejects credentials and URL query strings but accepts https://example.test/run#token=REDACTED-secret. The unchanged URI can be stored and returned to workspace readers despite the redacted-reference contract. The probe proves validation acceptance; it does not claim a live secret leak or remote evidence fetch.','Reject or safely redact URL fragments along with query credentials, for both HTTPS and URN references. Retain valid token-free evidence tests.'), +('P2','Completed verification evidence can be moved between runs','packages/db/migrations/0050_regional_verification_immutability.sql',19,'Reproduced against fresh PostgreSQL through direct SQL','After completing a run, UPDATE of its claim result to a second running run succeeds. The trigger checks NEW.run_id rather than protecting the old completed parent. The completed manifest remains recorded after evidence is removed. Current public API does not expose arbitrary run_id updates; this is a broken database immutability guarantee, not a demonstrated API privilege escalation.','Reject updates to run_id, workspace_id, namespaced_claim_id and originating_version_id; validate the old parent for updates/deletes. Test direct SQL mutation of completed evidence and normal updates within a running run.'), +('P2','Semantic ranges ignore older compatible published versions','packages/domain/src/composition-service.ts',242,'Code-traced','Both catalogs apply LIMIT 101 before JavaScript semver filtering. If the newest 101 versions are 2.x and ^1.0.0 matches an older published version, ids is empty and resolution falsely reports no compatible version. Exact pins have a SQL equality filter and avoid this specific case.','Page candidates until satisfying versions or an explicit bounded-search error are established; distinguish a search limit from an unsatisfied constraint. Add a 102-plus-version range fixture.') +],21:[ +('P1','Asset download outages bypass resilient fallback','packages/local-runtime/src/cloud-provider.ts',85,'Reproduced with mocked fetch rejection; Runtime.resolve branch traced','MCP retrieval can succeed and its authenticated asset download can then fail with a native TypeError or stream error. download() does not translate that error, while Runtime.resolve only permits fallback for specific RuntimeError codes. A resilient projection fails instead of using its verified local snapshot.','Map network, timeout and stream failures to CLOUD_UNAVAILABLE while preserving origin, size and digest validation errors. Test failure after successful MCP metadata retrieval through Runtime.resolve.'), +('P2','Network origin changes can bypass trust review','packages/local-runtime/src/trust.ts',29,'Reproduced trust-envelope comparison','Adding Destination: HTTPS://new.example.test/upload produces no network entry and trustExpands=false because the URL matcher is case sensitive. The launcher still instructs agents not to contact unlisted origins.','Recognize supported URL schemes case-insensitively and normalize origins, or reject unrecognized network declarations. Test uppercase HTTP(S), ws/wss, and unchanged-origin controls.'), +('P2','Sync retains explicitly deselected owned projections','packages/local-runtime/src/runtime.ts',161,'Reproduced with actual SQLite and filesystem','After projecting a skill and configuring target.skills=[], sync returns no plans but leaves the old discovery symlink and registry entry. Removing mounts, targets or aliases similarly leaves obsolete native commands available.','Reconcile the desired set against owned projections for the selected project/target and safely uninstall stale entries. Preserve unrelated user-managed files and projections owned by other project contexts.'), +('P2','Equivalent cloud endpoint spelling breaks profiles','packages/local-runtime/src/profiles.ts',152,'Reproduced with fake secret store','Profiles.add stores new URL(endpoint).href, adding a trailing slash for https://example.test. Add root URL, explicit slash and invalid endpoint tests.'), +('P2','Generated launchers lose a custom runtime home','packages/local-runtime/src/adapters.ts',92,'Reproduced generated output; CLI lookup traced','A runtime installed with --home/custom state produces commands containing only skillplane resolve ID. A later host invocation without SKILLPLANE_HOME opens the default store and cannot find that ID. Both live and cached CLI paths lose the documented home selection.','Carry a safely quoted absolute runtime home or stable installation locator into both launcher commands. Verify invocation after unsetting SKILLPLANE_HOME and changing cwd.'), +('P2','Exported upload API can send local-only workspace events','packages/local-runtime/src/analytics.ts',91,'Reproduced with callback capture and opt-in consent','UsageQueue.upload(send) treats an omitted workspace as a wildcard and passes local: events to the sender. Implementation documentation promises local workspace events remain local.','Require an explicit cloud workspace and reject local identities at the queue boundary. Retain opt-in consent and exact workspace filtering, and test omitted, local and foreign workspace cases.'), +('P2','Interrupted uninstall cannot recover its registry state','packages/local-runtime/src/projections.ts',289,'Reproduced filesystem/SQLite fault injection','uninstall removes the symlink before deleting the SQLite record. # PR #17 quality analysis **9/10 — Ready.** Reviewed `b87c6797328b0db5f21f724150b96e4f0aa7cc80`. GitHub state at final check: MERGED. Small coherent deletion of unused wrappers, retained production audit/redaction writers and listPage, and an exactly equivalent routingEpoch helper. The HTTP includeArchived compatibility shim remains. No actionable regression found within this cleanup. ## Scope and requirements Complete six-file cleanup diff and affected helper/caller contracts inspected. No database schema or UI behavior is changed; database/browser/deployment tests were not run for this cleanup. No linked Linear issue was present; the PR promise of no product behavior change is the scope authority. ## Scores
DimensionWeightScore / 10
Requirements fidelity30%9
Correctness and safety30%9
Architecture20%9
Verification15%8
Delivery5%9
Weighted result rounds to the nearest 0.5. Readiness blockers override the arithmetic. Compact change and reproduced compatibility support the score. ## Findings No actionable defects found in the reviewed cleanup. # PR #21 portable reproduction evidence

Analysis ID: f85af38e-c0bc-4438-983d-fde8c5197122. Exact source commit `cc34611f997c0eac391285aabce2c6912f88237c`; base and merge base `ad4308fa1f5bb3bfff043993ea162190d9375345`. Fixture SHA is the same reviewed PR head; fixture rows/bundles are synthetic.

126 existing unit tests passed (domain 32, mcp-schema 27, MCP 42, local-runtime 25). All 25 selected MCP read/resource-routing/local-provider/conformance integration tests passed. Seven independent desired-behavior probes failed with the documented defects. Runtime/domain/schema typechecks passed.

## Reproduction setup

Check out the exact SHA into a disposable checkout. Use Node 22.22.1, pnpm 11.9.0 and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. The review reused installed lockfile dependencies; it did not reinstall all dependencies. Run package test:unit scripts, not root-relative CLI tests (their CWD matters). The standalone installer is exercised by the local-runtime package test.

For the independent probes below, save `review-probes.test.ts` at the disposable repository root. Create a Vitest config with exact source aliases for each @skillplane package (and specific exported subpaths before parent aliases); set test.include to that file. This prevents workspace links from loading another checkout. Run `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config review.config.ts`. Expected exit: 1; defects are asserted against desired behavior.

## Probe source

Review-feedback disposition: PR #20 — feedback disposition. **6.5/10 provisional — Needs fixes.** Reviewed `2f47dd39058ea9c32fc13eefa413090dd8f0fcf0`. GitHub state at final check: OPEN. Substantial domain integration: immutable server-generated locks, semver/DAG bounds, normalized dependency storage, inherited namespaced claims, exact target attestations, independent-verifier identity checks, retention, UI/MCP authoring and explicit rollback controls. Existing negative evidence gates and lifecycle tests pass. ## Scope and requirements Broad source review of resolver, bundle validation, publication/revalidation, verification, migrations, MCP scope/read paths and UI composition contracts, guided by SKI-3 acceptance criteria and both design documents. Full browser flows, separate control/regional migration rollout, race schedules, production canaries, and exhaustive disposition of every lower-priority bot suggestion remain unverified. No full repository build/lint rerun in this assessment; author execution records report those separately. - [Architecture & Delivery Plan — SKI-3: Support native skill composition, dependency resolution, and verification modules](https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-3-support-native-skill-composition-7187021da718), updated 2026-08-04T13:56:53.581Z; document ID 8ede3c23-99c6-4f48-8af2-6ea73e5f5ef6; content SHA-256 `ef95dce18494b62a6de806f0e7f10991889e5c238bb49cd9a19b88ae7a55f82d`. - [Ideation & Product Rationale — SKI-3: Support native skill composition, dependency resolution, and verification modules](https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-3-support-native-skill-composition-d5eefcd2c7b6), updated 2026-08-04T13:56:56.934Z; document ID ff751d37-e9fd-4c65-af99-03c92b0ef431; content SHA-256 `e4e25f2d3bce49678b170bb48ec30edb4e1db4606d575a7b0e8a785294e072a9`. The issue and relation/comment surfaces were fetched live. No blocking issue relation was returned. The architecture requires independent verification, exact locks and public-closure authorization; the DataFn example explicitly rejects package-install-only evidence. ## Scores

The provisional score reflects strong foundations but confirmed boundary failures and incomplete live acceptance coverage. ## Findings ### F20-1 — P1: OAuth tokens bypass scopes for new composition tools Reproduced scope-map failure; authorization path traced. [mcp/src/server.ts:218](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/2f47dd39058ea9c32fc13eefa413090dd8f0fcf0/mcp/src/server.ts#L218). A user OAuth token lacking skills:write can reach skill_composition_candidate_create: requiredScopesForRequest returns \[\], and principalForWorkspace reconstructs a user principal from membership without retaining token scopes. The same missing-map pattern applies to all ten new tools. Service principals still receive domain scope checks; this finding specifically concerns user OAuth tokens. Required follow-up: Map all ten tools to read/write/publish scopes and test under-scoped user OAuth requests through the real HTTP boundary. The probe uses the actual registered tool name and separately confirms the user-principal path. ### F20-2 — P1: Global visibility withdrawal is ignored by regional bundle reads Reproduced with actual source method and mocked storage/control rows. [packages/domain/src/composition-service.ts:124](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/2f47dd39058ea9c32fc13eefa413090dd8f0fcf0/packages/domain/src/composition-service.ts#L124). When a global withdrawn_sequence exists while a regional skill row is still public, source() returns the regional canonical bundle to a foreign-workspace caller. The cutoff is checked only in the public-projection branch. This defeats the documented immediate global withdrawal guarantee during propagation or regional transaction failure. No production data was accessed. Required follow-up: Apply the causally ordered withdrawal gate to regional public reads too, using trusted visibility sequence state; retain authorized owner access. Test a committed global withdrawal with a stale regional public row and a newer legitimate republish. ### F20-3 — P2: New catalog exceeds the existing Linear client budget Reproduced over local MCP HTTP conformance. [mcp/src/server.ts:218](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/2f47dd39058ea9c32fc13eefa413090dd8f0fcf0/mcp/src/server.ts#L218). The new 37-tool catalog compacts to 41,678 bytes for the Linear OAuth client, above the existing 32,768-byte contract. Conformance fails on size and on the stale 27-tool inventory assertion. Updating the count alone leaves the compatibility regression. A live Linear connection was not exercised. Required follow-up: Reduce or partition the advertised client catalog while preserving required tool access, and update the complete inventory expectations. Keep the 32 KiB compatibility assertion and verify live Linear discovery. ### F20-4 — P2: A public parent can publish an archived public dependency Reproduced against fresh PostgreSQL. [packages/domain/src/composition-service.ts:410](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/2f47dd39058ea9c32fc13eefa413090dd8f0fcf0/packages/domain/src/composition-service.ts#L410). Creating a public child, archiving it, and creating a public parent in the same workspace succeeds. source() allows same-workspace archived pins; revalidate() checks visibility but not archive/public availability. Anonymous reads reject that archived child, so the newly published public parent cannot deliver its closure. Preserving private same-workspace archived pins is valid; publishing a publicly unusable closure is the defect. Required follow-up: For public parent creation/publication, validate anonymous/public availability for every node, including archive and withdrawal status. Keep private pinned archive semantics intact. ### F20-5 — P2: MCP rejects authorized unpublished composite retrieval Code-traced. [mcp/src/tools/retrieve.ts:97](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/2f47dd39058ea9c32fc13eefa413090dd8f0fcf0/mcp/src/tools/retrieve.ts#L97). resolveVersion authorizes a pending v2 candidate and resolves it with allowCandidate=true. skillRetrieve then resolves the same version again with the default false; skillResolve repeats this mismatch. Authors therefore cannot retrieve/resolve a candidate that the first authorization step explicitly admitted. Required follow-up: Pass the established candidate-read authorization through both final composition calls and add end-to-end owner candidate retrieval/resolve tests, plus viewer and foreign-principal denial controls. ### F20-6 — P2: Redacted evidence validation accepts token fragments Reproduced validation boundary with mocked idempotency replay. [packages/domain/src/verification.ts:273](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/2f47dd39058ea9c32fc13eefa413090dd8f0fcf0/packages/domain/src/verification.ts#L273). addEvidence rejects credentials and URL query strings but accepts [https://example.test/run#token=dummy-secret](https://example.test/run#token=dummy-secret). The unchanged URI can be stored and returned to workspace readers despite the redacted-reference contract. The probe proves validation acceptance; it does not claim a live secret leak or remote evidence fetch. Required follow-up: Reject or safely redact URL fragments along with query credentials, for both HTTPS and URN references. Retain valid token-free evidence tests. ### F20-7 — P2: Completed verification evidence can be moved between runs Reproduced against fresh PostgreSQL through direct SQL. [packages/db/migrations/0050_regional_verification_immutability.sql:19](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/2f47dd39058ea9c32fc13eefa413090dd8f0fcf0/packages/db/migrations/0050_regional_verification_immutability.sql#L19). After completing a run, UPDATE of its claim result to a second running run succeeds. The trigger checks [NEW.run](http://NEW.run)_id rather than protecting the old completed parent. The completed manifest remains recorded after evidence is removed. Current public API does not expose arbitrary run_id updates; this is a broken database immutability guarantee, not a demonstrated API privilege escalation. Required follow-up: Reject updates to run_id, workspace_id, namespaced_claim_id and originating_version_id; validate the old parent for updates/deletes. Test direct SQL mutation of completed evidence and normal updates within a running run. ### F20-8 — P2: Semantic ranges ignore older compatible published versions Code-traced. [packages/domain/src/composition-service.ts:242](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/blob/2f47dd39058ea9c32fc13eefa413090dd8f0fcf0/packages/domain/src/composition-service.ts#L242). Both catalogs apply LIMIT 101 before JavaScript semver filtering. If the newest 101 versions are 2.x and \^1.0.0 matches an older published version, ids is empty and resolution falsely reports no compatible version. Exact pins have a SQL equality filter and avoid this specific case. Required follow-up: Page candidates until satisfying versions or an explicit bounded-search error are established; distinguish a search limit from an unsatisfied constraint. Add a 102-plus-version range fixture. ## Validation and limits 135 existing unit tests passed (storage 18, mcp-schema 25, domain 45, MCP 47). Three focused database/MCP suites: 19 passed, 2 failed (catalog size and stale inventory). Five independent boundary probes: 3 desired-behavior failures, 2 controls passed. Two additional PostgreSQL probes both failed desired guarantees (archived public closure and completed evidence reassignment). Domain/storage/schema typechecks passed. Node 22.22.1, pnpm 11.9.0, Vitest 4.1.10, installed lockfile dependencies reused from the clean exact-head PR worktrees. Independent probes ran from git-archive snapshots with source aliases.
